questions.q: Put these phrases of the unit in the order of the text.
items: अस्मै च उपदिश्यमानं वयम् अपि उपधारयिष्यामः
questions.explain: They speak again, regard their view, Sushruta will ask, and what is taught to him they too will take up.

questions.q: In the invented line सः पठिष्यति, what does the verb mean?
optionExplain: Right: -ष्यति is a 3 sg. future like प्रक्ष्यति.
That needs -ष्यामः.
The form is future, not past.
That would be an imperative.
questions.explain: -ष्यति = he will; -ष्यामः = we shall.
questions.teaches: The ending -ष्यति is a third person singular future.

questions.q: What does the speaker say?
optionExplain: No time word occurs.
Right: एवम् अस्तु means so let it be.
Nothing negates it.
No such words occur.
questions.explain: The reply is agreement.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The words once the joins are opened.
questions.rule: ह is an indeclinable; उवाच is a perfect verb.

questions.q: Put the words in the order of the text.
questions.explain: He, indeed, said, so, let it be.
questions.teaches: The reply adds ह after सः.

questions.q: Which word does this unit have that the earlier short reply did not?
optionExplain: Both replies have एवम्.
Both replies have अस्तु.
Right: The earlier reply ran सः उवाच एवम् अस्तु.
Both replies have उवाच.
questions.explain: Only ह is added.

questions.q: Which splits of the joins in स होवाचैवमस्त्विति are right?
optionExplain: ऐ comes from अ/आ + ए, not अ + उ.
The final म् stands before the अ.
अ + ए = ऐ.
अ + उ = ओ.
questions.explain: The splits होवाच, उवाचैवम् and एवमस्तु are right; हैवाच mixes the vowels.
questions.rule: अ + उ = ओ; अ + ए = ऐ.

questions.q: By the same sandhi as ह + उवाच, what does तत्र + उवाच give?
optionExplain: The vowels do join.
ऐ comes from अ/आ + ए, not अ + उ.
ऊ would come from उ + उ.
Right: अ + उ = ओ.
questions.explain: अ + उ = ओ.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: अ + उ joins into ओ.

questions.q: The text says the purpose of Ayurveda is protection of whom?
optionExplain: Right: स्वस्थस्य रक्षणम् says this.
No learned person occurs in the line.
No wealthy person occurs in the line.
Only Suśruta is addressed, not as a purpose.
questions.explain: रक्षणम् is protection; स्वस्थस्य is of the healthy.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the unit.
questions.rule: वत्स is a vocative; स्वस्थस्य is a genitive.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the unit in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Address; the purpose; the afflicted; their release from disease; protection of the healthy.
questions.teaches: The purpose sentence runs in this order.

questions.q: Which two purposes of Ayurveda does the unit state?
options: Increase of wealth for the physician.
Release from disease of those afflicted by disease.
optionExplain: No such purpose is stated.
Stated first.
No such purpose is stated.
Stated second.
questions.explain: The unit gives exactly these two purposes.

questions.q: The second purpose is the ____ (protection) of the healthy. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: रक्षणम् is the neuter noun: protection.
questions.teaches: रक्षणम् = protection.

questions.q: In the invented phrase बालस्य रक्षणम्, what does बालस्य mean?
optionExplain: That would be a dative form.
Right: -स्य is the genitive, as in स्वस्थस्य.
That would be an instrumental form.
That would be an ablative form.
questions.explain: The genitive -स्य says of.
questions.teaches: The genitive singular -स्य says whose.

questions.q: The text explains the name Ayurveda by what word-play?
options: Life is lost in it, or by it one loses life.
Life is told in it, or by it one tells life.
Life is found in it, or by it one finds life.
Life is ended in it, or by it one ends life.
optionExplain: The verbs mean found and finds, not lose.
Neither verb means tell.
Right: विद्यते and विन्दति give the two senses.
Neither verb means end.
questions.explain: Both explanations use √vid with आयुः.
questions.rule: विद्यते = is found; विन्दति = one finds.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the explanation.
questions.rule: अस्मिन् is locative; अनेन is instrumental.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the unit in the order of the text.
questions.explain: First explanation, second explanation after वा, then the name.
questions.teaches: Two explanations end in the name.

questions.q: In the second explanation, what does अनेन do?
optionExplain: That is अस्मिन्, used in the first explanation.
That would be a genitive.
That would be an ablative.
Right: अनेन is the instrumental: by this.
questions.explain: अनेन = by this; अस्मिन् = in this.

questions.q: The second explanation uses the verb ____ (one finds). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अनेन वा आयुः विन्दति: by this one finds life.
questions.teaches: विन्दति = one finds.
questions.rule: The second explanation uses विन्दति, the first विद्यते.

questions.q: In the invented line अनेन ज्ञानं विन्दति, what does the line mean?
optionExplain: Right: अनेन = by this; विन्दति = one finds.
That would use अस्मिन् and विद्यते.
विन्दति does not mean lose.
अनेन is not a genitive.
questions.explain: अनेन + विन्दति = by this one finds.
questions.teaches: Instrumental अनेन with विन्दति: by this one finds.

questions.q: The unit says the first limb is stated without contradiction from what?
optionExplain: Wealth and anger are not in the compound.
Right: The four words of the compound.
Fear and speech are not in the compound.
These are not the four words.
questions.explain: प्रत्यक्ष-आगम-अनुमान-उपमानैः.

questions.q: Match each word of the compound to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four glosses on the card.
questions.rule: The four stand in one द्वन्द्व compound.

questions.q: Put the four in the order of the compound.
questions.explain: Perception, tradition, inference, analogy.
questions.teaches: The four means of knowing stand in a fixed order.

questions.q: What does अविरुद्धम् mean here?
optionExplain: अ- negates, it does not strengthen.
Nothing is said of proof.
Right: अ- negates विरुद्धम्, contradicted.
The next word, उच्यमानम्, says it is being stated.
questions.explain: अ + विरुद्धम् = not contradicted.

questions.q: Which readings of प्रत्यक्षागमानुमानोपमानैः अविरुद्धम् fit the unit?
optionExplain: अ- negates: the word says not contradicted.
आगम is one of the four; -ऐः = by, अ- = not.
उपमान is one of the four; -ऐः = by, अ- = not.
-ऐः makes perception the means by which, not the thing contradicted.
questions.explain: The four are the means by which the limb is not contradicted.

questions.q: In the invented phrase शास्त्रैः अविरुद्धम्, what does it mean?
optionExplain: अ- negates the contradiction.
-ऐः means by, and अविरुद्ध means not contradicted, not not stated.
-ऐः is not a dative.
Right: -ऐः = by (plural); अ- = not, as in the unit.
questions.explain: -ऐः = by; अविरुद्धम् = not contradicted.
questions.teaches: Instrumental plural -ऐः with अविरुद्धम्: not contradicted by.

questions.q: According to the unit, who cut off the head of the sacrifice?
optionExplain: Right: रुद्रेण यज्ञस्य शिरश्छिन्नम्.
Indra is propitiated by the gods, not named as the cutter.
They are asked to join it.
They approach the Ashvins.
questions.explain: रुद्रेण is the instrumental agent of छिन्नम्.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the story.
questions.rule: छिन्नम् and संहितम् are past participles.

questions.q: Put these events in the order in which the text tells them.
questions.explain: Cut; the gods approach the two; they agree; Indra is propitiated; the head is joined.
questions.teaches: The story follows this order.

questions.q: Whom do the gods approach after the head is cut off?
optionExplain: He is the cutter in the story.
Right: देवा अश्विनौ अभिगम्य ऊचुः.
Indra is propitiated later.
He is not in this story.
questions.explain: अश्विनौ is the object of अभिगम्य.

questions.q: Which figures does the story name?
optionExplain: Not named in the story.
Named as the cutter.
Named as the ones approached.
Named as the one propitiated.
questions.explain: The story names Rudra, the Ashvins and Indra.

questions.q: In the invented line बालेन फलं छिन्नम्, who does the cutting?
optionExplain: फलम् is what is cut.
-एन is not a dative.
Right: The instrumental बालेन names the agent, as रुद्रेण does.
बालेन names the doer.
questions.explain: The instrumental names the agent of छिन्नम्.
questions.teaches: With a passive participle, the doer stands in the instrumental.

questions.q: What does the unit say about this branch among the eight?
options: It is held equal to the rest.
It is held the least used.
optionExplain: अधिकम् means foremost, not lowest.
एव alone excludes equality.
अधिकम् is not least.
Right: एतदेव अधिकम् अभिमतम्.
questions.explain: एतत् एव अधिकम् = this alone foremost.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four items of the compound.
questions.rule: The four are joined as a list in one compound.

questions.q: Put the four items in the order of the compound.
questions.explain: Instruments, blades, caustic, fire.
questions.teaches: The four items stand in a fixed order.

questions.q: What is the last reason the unit gives, after the list of means?
options: It is common to all branches.
It is rare among all branches.
It is hidden from all branches.
It is opposed to all branches.
optionExplain: Right: सर्वतन्त्रसामान्यात् says this.
सामान्य is common, not rare.
Nothing is said of hiding.
सामान्य is not opposed.
questions.explain: सर्वतन्त्रसामान्यात् = from being common to all branches.

questions.q: Which of these does the unit name among the means applied?
optionExplain: A charm is not named.
Instruments.
Blades.
Fire.
questions.explain: The compound names instruments, blades, caustic and fire.

questions.q: In the invented phrase शीलात् मान्यः, what does शीलात् give?
optionExplain: That would be a genitive.
Right: -आत् gives a reason, as in सर्वतन्त्रसामान्यात्.
That would be an instrumental.
That would be a dative.
questions.explain: The ablative -आत् gives because of.
questions.teaches: The ablative -आत् gives a reason.

questions.q: Which of these does the text say the subject provides?
optionExplain: No kingdom is named in the line.
No dwelling is named in the line.
Right: वृत्तिकरम् means providing livelihood.
No weapon is named in the line.
questions.explain: The last quality of the list is वृत्तिकरम्: providing a livelihood.

questions.q: Put the six qualities in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: Eternal, meritorious, conducive to heaven, to fame, to long life, providing livelihood.

questions.q: Match each quality to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the six qualities with their glosses on the card.
questions.teaches: The qualities of the line and their plain meanings.

questions.q: Which of these words mean conducive to something, by the card?
optionExplain: Glossed providing livelihood, not conducive to anything.
Glossed eternal, not conducive to anything.
Glossed conducive to long life.
Glossed conducive to heaven.
questions.explain: The card gives conducive to for स्वर्ग्यम्, यशस्यम् and आयुष्यम्; the other two are glossed differently.
questions.rule: Conducive to is the gloss of -य words here.

questions.q: Which split is right for तदिदम् in the line?
optionExplain: No word तस् is given on the card.
The card gives तत्, not ता.
There is no word दम् in the line.
Right: The card splits it into तत् (that) and इदम् (this).
questions.explain: तदिदम् = तत् + इदम्: the final त् turns into द् before the vowel.
questions.rule: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel.

questions.q: By the rule of तत् + इदम् = तदिदम्, what does तत् + अपि give?
optionExplain: Right: Final त् becomes द् before the vowel अ.
The vowel cannot simply vanish.
त् does not turn into थ् here.
The final त् does not drop away.
questions.explain: As in तदिदम्, a final त् before a vowel becomes द्: तदपि.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a vowel.

questions.q: Who is the first in the chain to have declared it?
optionExplain: Indra comes fourth, after the two Ashvins.
Right: ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच: Brahma declared it.
Prajapati learned it from Brahma.
The Ashvins come third.
questions.explain: The line opens with ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच: Brahma declared.

questions.q: Put the teachers in the order in which the lineage names them.
questions.explain: Brahma, Prajapati, the two Ashvins, Indra.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: for the sake of the welfare of beings
questions.explain: Four words of the line with their glosses on the card.
questions.rule: अर्थिभ्यः is dative plural; प्रजाहितहेतोः is a compound used like a word meaning for the sake of.
questions.teaches: Key words of the lineage and of the purpose.

questions.q: Which words are in the ablative (from whom)?
optionExplain: Dative plural: to seekers.
Nominative dual: the Ashvins as learners.
Ablative dual: from the two Ashvins.
Ablative singular: from him.
questions.explain: The card marks तस्मात् and अश्विभ्याम् as ablative; अश्विनौ is nominative and अर्थिभ्यः dative.

questions.q: To whom, and for what purpose, does the text say it is to be imparted?
options: To kings, for the sake of glory.
To pupils only, in return for a fee.
To seekers, for the welfare of beings.
To the gods, for the sake of sacrifice.
optionExplain: Neither kings nor glory appear.
No fee is mentioned.
Right: अर्थिभ्यः प्रजाहितहेतोः says exactly this.
Neither gods nor sacrifice appear.
questions.explain: The recipients are seekers and the purpose is the welfare of beings.
questions.rule: Dative = to whom; हेतोः = for the sake of.

questions.q: In the invented देवदत्तः यज्ञदत्तात् पाठम् अधीते (learns), from whom does Devadatta learn?
optionExplain: The subject is Devadatta, not the source.
पाठम् is the object, the thing learned.
The ablative names a source.
Right: -आत् marks the ablative: the one learned from.
questions.explain: The ablative यज्ञदत्तात् names the source, as तस्मात् names Prajapati in the text.
questions.teaches: The ablative case names the one from whom something is learned.

questions.q: How does the speaker name himself in the first line?
options: Indra, the king of the gods.
optionExplain: Right: धन्वन्तरिः आदिदेवः.
The card names Dhanvantari, not Brahma.
The card names Dhanvantari, not Indra.
The card names Dhanvantari, not Sushruta.
questions.explain: The first line says अहं हि धन्वन्तरिः आदिदेवः.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Who he is, the first god, remover for the immortals, the limb joined with other limbs, arrived on earth again, to teach here.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse with their glosses on the card.
questions.rule: उपदेष्टुम् is an infinitive; अमराणाम् is genitive plural.
questions.teaches: The key words of the verse.

questions.q: Which words are accusative singular (marked acc. sg. on the card)?
optionExplain: Genitive plural: of the immortals.
Instrumental plural: with limbs.
f. acc. sg.: the earth.
n. acc. sg.: the branch he teaches.
questions.explain: शल्याङ्गम् and गाम् are marked acc. sg.; the other two are instrumental and genitive plural.
questions.rule: Accusative = the object, or the place reached.

questions.q: Which split is right for प्राप्तोऽस्मि?
optionExplain: The card's word is प्राप्तः with a visarga.
Right: The card gives प्राप्तः (arrived) and अस्मि (I am).
ओ is not a separate word here.
The word अस्मि is not cut in two.
questions.explain: After अ, a visarga becomes ओ before अ, and that अ is replaced by ऽ: प्राप्तः + अस्मि = प्राप्तोऽस्मि.

questions.q: By the sandhi in इह + उपदेष्टुम् = इहोपदेष्टुम्, what does तत्र + उवाच give?
optionExplain: अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
The अ does not vanish; they merge into ओ.
Right: अ + उ joins into ओ.
These two vowels do join.
questions.explain: As in इहोपदेष्टुम्, अ + उ = ओ.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: अ or आ followed by उ joins into ओ.

questions.q: What is called puruṣa in this treatise?
options: A single sage who composed all of this treatise.
The stationary world apart from moving beings.
The five elements taken apart from any being.
Beings made of the five great elements, together.
optionExplain: No author is named in the passage.
The passage does not say this.
It speaks of beings made of them.
Right: पञ्चमहाभूतशरीरिसमवायः पुरुष इत्युच्यते.
questions.explain: The first sentence defines puruṣa as the union of beings made of the five great elements.

questions.q: Put the four classes of beings in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: Sweat-born, womb-born, egg-born, sprout-born.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The two pairs of the twofold world, with the glosses on the card.
questions.rule: Each pair is said of the world; the text calls the world twofold in both ways.
questions.teaches: The two pairs by which the world is called twofold.

questions.q: Among the things the text mentions here, which does it call प्रधान (chief)?
optionExplain: Right: तत्र पुरुषः प्रधानम्.
The text calls this the other, not the chief.
It is never called chief.
It is never called chief.
questions.explain: The text says among them the puruṣa is the chief; the other is his instrument.

questions.q: Which split is right for पुरुषोऽधिष्ठानम्?
optionExplain: The word is पुरुषः with a visarga.
Right: The card gives पुरुषः and अधिष्ठानम्.
ओ is not a word here.
The word अधिष्ठानम् keeps its first letter.
questions.explain: After अ, a visarga becomes ओ before अ, and that अ is replaced by ऽ.

questions.q: By the pattern of संस्वेदज (sweat-born) and अण्डज (egg-born), what does जलज mean?
optionExplain: -ज does not mean giving.
-ज does not mean drinking.
Right: -ज at the end means born from, here from water.
-ज does not mean loving.
questions.explain: The ending -ज means born from: जल + ज = born from water.
questions.teaches: -ज at the end of a compound means born from.

questions.q: What does the text say are called diseases (व्याधि)?
optionExplain: संयोग is joining, not separating.
The word is दुःख, suffering.
The elements are not named here.
Right: तद्दुःखसंयोगाः व्याधयः उच्यन्ते.
questions.explain: The sentence says the conjunctions with suffering are called व्याधि.

questions.q: Put the parts of the sentence in the order of the text.
questions.explain: That, suffering, conjunctions, diseases, are called.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the sentence with their glosses on the card.
questions.rule: उच्यन्ते is a passive plural verb: they are called.
questions.teaches: The key words of the sentence.

questions.q: Which rendering keeps all four words right, leaving aside whose suffering?
options: The conjunctions with suffering are called diseases.
The separations from suffering are called diseases.
The conjunctions with pleasure are called diseases.
The conjunctions with suffering are called remedies.
optionExplain: Right: It follows तद्दुःखसंयोगाः व्याधयः उच्यन्ते.
संयोग means conjunction, not separation.
The word is दुःख, not pleasure.
The word is व्याधि, not remedy.
questions.explain: Only the first rendering keeps all four words right.
questions.rule: Check each word against the card.

questions.q: Why is the first word written तद्दुःख and not तत्दुःख?
options: Final त् becomes न् before the voiced द.
Final त् becomes द् before the voiced द.
Final त् is dropped before the voiced द.
द is added to mark the plural.
optionExplain: त् never turns into a nasal here.
Right: A voiced sound follows, so त् turns voiced.
The consonant remains, as द्.
The plural is shown by -आः in संयोगाः.
questions.explain: A voiced consonant follows, so the final त् is voiced to द्.

questions.q: By the rule of तद्दुःख, what does तत् + गृहम् give?
optionExplain: The sandhi is not left undone.
त् does not become न् here.
Right: त् becomes द् before the voiced ग.
त् does not copy the next consonant.
questions.explain: ग is a voiced consonant, so the final त् becomes द्.
questions.teaches: A final त् becomes द् before a voiced consonant.

questions.q: What division does the text give of the diseases?
options: They are of one kind only.
optionExplain: The word is चतुर्विध, fourfold.
The word is चतुर्विध, fourfold.
The text speaks of several kinds.
Right: ते चतुर्विधाः says this.
questions.explain: चतुर्विधाः means of four kinds.

questions.q: Put the four kinds in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: Adventitious, bodily, mental, natural.

questions.q: Match each kind to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four kinds with their glosses on the card.
questions.rule: All four are masculine nominative plural.
questions.teaches: The four kinds of diseases and their plain meanings.

questions.q: Which of these are among the four kinds the text names?
optionExplain: Not among the four named.
Not among the four named.
Named third: mental.
Named first: adventitious.
questions.explain: Only आगन्तवः and मानसाः are in the list of four.

questions.q: Which split is right for स्वाभाविकाश्चेति?
optionExplain: Right: The card gives स्वाभाविकाः, च and इति.
श्च is not a word; the visarga is lost in this split.
The word is इति, not एति.
There is no word श on the card.
questions.explain: The visarga turns into श् before च, and च + इ joins into चे.

questions.q: By the rule of स्वाभाविकाः + च = स्वाभाविकाश्च, what does वृक्षाः + च give?
optionExplain: The visarga cannot just vanish.
Right: The visarga becomes श् before च.
The sandhi is not left undone.
The visarga turns into श्, not ष्.
questions.explain: A visarga before च becomes श्, as in स्वाभाविकाश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च becomes श्.

questions.q: Which of the four kinds does this unit take up?
optionExplain: The word शारीराः does not occur here.
The word मानसाः does not occur here.
Right: आगन्तवः is the subject.
The word स्वाभाविकाः does not occur here.
questions.explain: The unit speaks of आगन्तवः, the adventitious ones.

questions.q: Put the parts of the sentence in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Of these, the adventitious ones, injury, caused by.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three parts of the sentence with their glosses on the card.
questions.teaches: The parts of the one-line definition.

questions.q: One word of this rendering is wrong: Of these, the adventitious ones are caused by food. Which word?
optionExplain: तेषाम् does mean of these.
आगन्तवः does mean adventitious ones.
निमित्ताः does mean caused by.
Right: The text says injury (अभिघात), not food.
questions.explain: The cause named is injury, so the word food is the error.

questions.q: Which split is right for तेषामागन्तवोऽभिघातनिमित्ताः?
optionExplain: Right: The card gives these three words.
The word is तेषाम् with म्.
The word keeps its first letter अ.
The word is आगन्तवः with its initial आ.
questions.explain: तेषाम् + आगन्तवः joins म् to आ; आगन्तवः + अभिघात becomes आगन्तवोऽभिघात.

questions.q: By the pattern of अभिघातनिमित्ताः (caused by injury), what does शोकनिमित्ताः mean?
optionExplain: निमित्त does not mean beyond.
Right: X-निमित्त means caused by X.
निमित्त does not mean free from.
निमित्त does not mean together with.
questions.explain: The first part names the cause: शोक + निमित्त = caused by grief.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrihi in -निमित्त means caused by the first part.

questions.q: Where does the text say the bodily diseases are rooted?
optionExplain: Injury is the cause of the adventitious kind.
These are not named in this unit.
Right: अन्नपानमूलाः: rooted in food and drink.
These are not named in this unit.
questions.explain: अन्नपानमूलाः means rooted in food and drink.

questions.q: Put the first four items of the list that is said to be out of balance in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Vata, Pitta, Kapha, blood.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the sentence with their meaning on the card.
questions.rule: वैषम्य is taken as unevenness, imbalance.
questions.teaches: Key words of the sentence.

questions.q: Which of these are named in the list of things whose imbalance is spoken of?
optionExplain: Not named in the list.
Not named in the list.
Named third.
Named first.
questions.explain: Only वात and कफ are in the list; the other two are not named.

questions.q: Which split is right for शारीरास्त्वन्नपानमूलाः?
optionExplain: The word is शारीराः with a visarga.
The word keeps its initial अ.
The last word is अन्नपानमूलाः whole.
Right: The card gives शारीराः, तु and अन्नपानमूलाः.
questions.explain: The visarga turns into स् before त; तु + अ turns into त्व.

questions.q: By the rule of शारीराः + तु = शारीरास्तु, what does बालाः + तु give?
optionExplain: Right: The visarga becomes स् before त.
श् is for च; before त the visarga gives स्.
The visarga cannot just vanish.
The sandhi is not left undone.
questions.explain: A visarga before त becomes स्, as in शारीरास्तु.
questions.teaches: A visarga before त becomes स्.

questions.q: The mental ones are linked with the divisions of which two?
optionExplain: These belong to the bodily kind.
Right: इच्छाद्वेषभेदैः.
These belong to the adventitious kind.
The text names desire and aversion.
questions.explain: The sentence ends with इच्छाद्वेषभेदैः: through the divisions of desire and aversion.

questions.q: Put the first six states of the list in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Anger, grief, fear, elation, despondency, jealousy.

questions.q: Match each state to its plain meaning.
questions.explain: Four states of the list with their plain meanings.
questions.rule: These four have plain, undisputed senses.
questions.teaches: Four states of the list and their meanings.

questions.q: Which of these are named in the list of mental ones?
optionExplain: Not in this list.
Not in this list.
Named third in the list.
Named first in the list.
questions.explain: क्रोध and भय are in the list; the other two are not named here.

questions.q: Why is the last part written भेदैर्भवन्ति with र्?
options: The visarga after ऐ becomes ओ before the voiced भ.
The visarga after ऐ becomes श् before the voiced भ.
The visarga after ऐ becomes र् before the voiced भ.
The visarga after ऐ is dropped before the voiced भ.
optionExplain: ओ is for a visarga after अ.
श् is for a visarga before च.
Right: A voiced sound follows a visarga that is not after अ.
It remains, as र्.
questions.explain: After a vowel other than अ or आ, a visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound.
questions.rule: Visarga after ऐ + voiced sound gives र्.

questions.q: By the rule of भेदैः + भवन्ति = भेदैर्भवन्ति, what does मित्रैः + वदन्ति give?
optionExplain: श् is for a visarga before च.
The visarga cannot just vanish.
The sandhi is not left undone.
Right: The visarga becomes र् before the voiced व.
questions.explain: After ऐ, a visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound.
questions.rule: Visarga after ऐ + voiced sound gives र्.
questions.teaches: A visarga after a vowel other than अ or आ becomes र् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: Which of these is named among the natural ones?
optionExplain: Right: जरा is in the list.
No wound is named in the list.
No fever is named in the list.
No burn is named in the list.
questions.explain: Old age (जरा) is the third item of the list.

questions.q: Put the five items in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: Hunger, thirst, old age, death, sleep.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The five items of the list with their glosses on the card.
questions.rule: All five are plain nouns joined in a single compound.
questions.teaches: The five natural conditions.

questions.q: Which split is right for स्वाभाविकास्तु?
optionExplain: स्तु is not a word on the card.
Right: The card gives स्वाभाविकाः and तु.
The word is तु, not स्तु.
The word is तु with a short vowel.
questions.explain: The visarga turns into स् before त.

questions.q: One word of this rendering is wrong: The natural ones are hunger, thirst, old age, birth, sleep and the like. Which word?
optionExplain: क्षुत् does mean hunger.
पिपासा does mean thirst.
Right: The text says मृत्यु: death.
निद्रा does mean sleep.
questions.explain: The fourth item is death, not birth.

questions.q: By the dvandva pattern of क्षुत्पिपासा, what does the invented सुखदुःखे mean?
optionExplain: A dvandva does not mean without.
A dvandva does not give an order in time.
A dvandva does not name a cause.
Right: A dvandva joins items with and.
questions.explain: A dvandva lists items as A and B in one word: सुख + दुःख = pleasure and pain.
questions.rule: Dvandva = A and B joined in one word.
questions.teaches: A dvandva compound joins items with and.

questions.q: What is the seat of these diseases, by the unit?
optionExplain: Right: मनःशरीराधिष्ठानाः.
The text names mind as well.
The text names body as well.
These are not named in this unit.
questions.explain: The compound says mind and body are their seat.

questions.q: Put the parts of the sentence in the order of the text.
questions.explain: They, these, mind, body, seat.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the sentence with their meaning.
questions.rule: मनः and शरीर are the first two members of the compound.
questions.teaches: The words of the definition of the seat.

questions.q: Which split is right for त एते at the start?
optionExplain: The word is ते, not तः.
Right: The card gives ते and एते.
The word is ते, not ता.
त is not a word on the card.
questions.explain: ते + एते joins as त एते: the ए of ते becomes अ before a vowel other than अ.
questions.rule: Final ए + a vowel other than अ gives अ + that vowel.

questions.q: In the compound, which part means seat?
optionExplain: The card glosses it as mind.
The card glosses it as body.
Right: The card glosses it as seat.
The card glosses it as these.
questions.explain: अधिष्ठान is the last member and means seat.

questions.q: By the rule of ते + एते = त एते, what does ते + इह give?
optionExplain: The vowels do not merge into ए.
ए does not become ई here.
ए does not become ऐ here.
Right: A final ए before a vowel other than अ becomes अ.
questions.explain: As in त एते, the final ए of ते becomes अ before the vowel इ.
questions.rule: Final ए + a vowel other than अ gives अ + that vowel.
questions.teaches: A final ए before a vowel other than अ becomes अ.

questions.q: What does the text say these four are?
optionExplain: Right: निग्रहहेतवः.
The text calls them means of checking.
The text calls them means of checking.
The seat is mind and body, in the previous unit.
questions.explain: निग्रहहेतवः: means of checking.
questions.rule: हेतु = means (in निग्रहहेतवः: means of checking).

questions.q: Put the four means in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: Purification, pacification, diet, conduct.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four means with their glosses on the card.
questions.rule: All four are members of one dvandva compound.
questions.teaches: The four means and their plain meanings.

questions.q: Which of these are named among the four means?
optionExplain: Not named in this unit.
Not named in this unit.
Named third.
Named first.
questions.explain: Only संशोधन and आहार are among the four means.

questions.q: On what condition does the text call them means of checking?
options: When they are applied only once.
When they are applied by a king.
When they are applied in the morning.
optionExplain: No number of times is given.
Right: सम्यक्प्रयुक्ताः says this.
No king is named.
No time of day is given.
questions.explain: सम्यक् means properly and प्रयुक्ताः means applied.

questions.q: By the pattern of निग्रहहेतवः (means of checking), what does the invented धनहेतवः mean?
optionExplain: हेतु does not mean lover.
हेतु does not mean enemy.
Right: X-हेतु names what the means is for.
हेतु does not mean free from.
questions.explain: As निग्रह + हेतवः is means of checking, धन + हेतवः is means of wealth.
questions.teaches: X-हेतु means a means of X.

questions.q: What does the text say the tastes rest on?
optionExplain: It is food that depends on the tastes.
Strength is not named as a support.
The moving is a class of oṣadhis.
Right: रसाः द्रव्याश्रयाः: the tastes rest on substances.
questions.explain: रसाः पुनः द्रव्याश्रयाः: the tastes in turn rest on substances.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the passage in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Food as root, of strength and the rest, depends on the tastes, tastes on substances, substances are oṣadhis, twofold.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the passage with their glosses on the card.
questions.teaches: The links of the chain and their meanings.

questions.q: Of which things does the text say food is the root, besides living beings?
optionExplain: Not named in this passage.
Not named in this passage.
Ojas is named.
Strength is named.
questions.explain: Food is the root of living beings and of strength, complexion and ojas.

questions.q: Which word does तास्तु (feminine plural) point back to?
optionExplain: Right: ओषधयः is feminine plural on the card.
द्रव्याणि is neuter.
रसाः is masculine.
आहारः is masculine and singular.
questions.explain: तास्तु is feminine plural, so it agrees only with ओषधयः.
questions.rule: A pronoun agrees in gender and number.

questions.q: By the rule of रसेषु + आयत्तः = रसेष्वायत्तः, what does साधु + इति give?
optionExplain: The sandhi is not left undone.
Right: Final उ before a vowel becomes व्.
उ + इ do not merge into ऊ.
उ + इ do not merge into ए.
questions.explain: As in रसेष्वायत्तः, a final उ becomes व् before a vowel: साध्विति.
questions.rule: Final उ + vowel gives व् + vowel.
questions.teaches: A final उ before a vowel becomes व्.

questions.q: Which class does the text say bears both flowers and fruit?
optionExplain: These bear fruit without flowers.
These are marked by spreading tendrils and clumps.
Right: पुष्पफलवन्तो वृक्षाः: those bearing flowers and fruit.
These are marked by ending when the fruit ripens.
questions.explain: The text gives the flower-and-fruit class the name वृक्ष.

questions.q: Match each class to the mark the text gives it.
questions.explain: The four classes and the marks the verse gives them.
questions.rule: Each class is defined by its own phrase in the second line.

questions.q: Put the four classes in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The first line names them: वनस्पति, वृक्ष, वीरुध, ओषधि.
questions.teaches: The four classes of stationary things, in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which classes does the text describe by something about fruit?
optionExplain: Fruit-bearing without flowers.
Flower-and-fruit bearing.
Marked by tendrils and clumps, with no word on fruit.
Their end comes with the ripening of fruit.
questions.explain: Three classes carry a fruit phrase; the वीरुध phrase speaks of growth form only.

questions.q: Which word in the verse means without flowers?
optionExplain: This means bearing flowers and fruit.
This means having spreading tendrils.
This means clump-forming.
Right: अ + पुष्प: not flowering.
questions.explain: अपुष्पाः is अ- plus पुष्प, with the negative अ-.
questions.rule: अ- negates the word after it.

questions.q: On the pattern of अपुष्पाः (without flowers), what does अफलाः mean?
optionExplain: Right: अ + फल, as अ + पुष्प.
The negative अ- removes, not gives.
Nothing in the word speaks of ripeness.
The prefix does not mean many.
questions.explain: अ- before a consonant says not; अफलाः = those without fruit.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- makes a word mean without or not.

questions.q: Which creatures does the text place among the egg-born?
options: Worms, insects and ants and the like
optionExplain: These stand under the womb-born.
Right: खगसर्पसरीसृपप्रभृतयोऽण्डजाः.
These stand under the sweat-born.
These stand under the sprout-born.
questions.explain: The egg-born (अण्डज) are birds, snakes, creeping creatures and the like.

questions.q: Match each creature to the kind the text puts it under.
questions.explain: One example from each of the four lists.

questions.q: Put the four kinds in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The first line runs: womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born, sprout-born.
questions.teaches: The four kinds of moving things, in the order of the text.

questions.q: What does the ending ज mean in जरायुज, अण्डज, स्वेदज and उद्भिज्ज?
optionExplain: No word of living on or feeding appears.
The ending names origin, not direction.
Right: जरायु, अण्ड, स्वेद, उद्भिद् + ज: born of each.
The ending names origin, not sight.
questions.explain: The four names are built on -ज, born from womb, egg, sweat and sprout.

questions.q: Which two creatures does the text put in the same kind?
optionExplain: Humans are womb-born, birds egg-born.
Ants are sweat-born, frogs sprout-born.
Worms are sweat-born, snakes egg-born.
Right: Both are in the egg-born list.
questions.explain: खग and सर्प both stand in the egg-born list.
questions.rule: Each list names its own creatures.

questions.q: On the pattern of स्वेदजाः (sweat-born), what does जलजाः mean?
optionExplain: Right: जल (water) + ज (born).
जल is water, not earth.
The ending is born, not given.
The ending is born, not going.
questions.explain: जल + ज builds born of water, as स्वेद + ज is born of sweat.
questions.teaches: -ज after a noun makes a word meaning born of that noun.

questions.q: Which of these does the text name as useful from the moving ones?
optionExplain: Roots come from the stationary ones.
Right: जङ्गमेभ्यश्चर्मनखरोमरुधिरादयः.
Leaves come from the stationary ones.
Bulbs come from the stationary ones.
questions.explain: Nails are in the list for the moving ones.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five parts named in the verse.
questions.rule: पत्र, मूल, कन्द come from stationary ones; नख, रुधिर from moving ones.

questions.q: Put these stationary-source items in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The list runs: leaf, flower, fruit, root, bulb.
questions.teaches: The parts of stationary things named as useful, in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which are named as useful from the moving ones?
optionExplain: Fruit: listed among the stationary ones.
Root: listed among the stationary ones.
Hair: in the list for the moving ones.
Hide: in the list for the moving ones.
questions.explain: Hide and hair stand in the moving list; root and fruit in the stationary list.
questions.rule: Check which list each word stands in.

questions.q: Which word of the verse means from the moving ones?
optionExplain: This is the plain plural, not from.
This is the genitive: of.
Right: It has the ending that means from.
This is the locative: among.
questions.explain: The verse names the moving ones with the word that means from them.

questions.q: On the pattern of स्थावरेभ्यः (from the stationary ones), what does वृक्षेभ्यः mean?
optionExplain: Of would end in -आणाम्.
Among would end in -एषु.
A plain plural would end in -आः.
Right: The ending -एभ्यः means from.
questions.explain: वृक्ष + एभ्यः = from the trees, like स्थावर + एभ्यः.
questions.teaches: The plural ending -एभ्यः means from.

questions.q: What does the word पार्थिवाः call the things listed?
optionExplain: Right: पार्थिवाः: earthy ones.
That was the name in the earlier units.
Not what पार्थिवाः says.
That is a different class of things.
questions.explain: पार्थिवाः is glossed earthy ones: things of the earth.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four of the substances named.
questions.rule: These are the first four items of the list.

questions.q: Put these items in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The list runs: gold, silver, gem, pearl, manahshila.
questions.teaches: The first items of the list of earthy substances, in the order of the text.

questions.q: What does आदयः at the end of the list tell us?
options: The list is closed; nothing else is meant
The list goes on: and so on
The last item named is the best
The items are named in a verb form
optionExplain: That would need a word like only.
Right: आदि = and so on, beginning with.
No ranking is stated.
आदयः is a noun form.
questions.explain: आदयः marks the list as open.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse name among the earthy ones?
optionExplain: Cold: a time-made condition, not an earthy one.
Nails: listed with the moving ones, not here.
Gem: the third item.
Gold: the first item.
questions.explain: Gold and gem are in this list; nails and cold belong to other lists.
questions.rule: Check each against the list in this unit.

questions.q: In the list compound सुवर्णरजतमणिमुक्ता (gold and silver and gem and pearl) the members are joined by and. What does the invented compound मुक्तारजतसुवर्णानि mean?
optionExplain: The members are joined by and, not of.
No member describes another.
Right: A list compound joins members with and, in any order.
No member owns another.
questions.explain: In such a list compound each member stands alone, joined by and.
questions.teaches: A list compound (dvandva) means its members together, joined by and.

questions.q: Which word in the unit means made by time?
optionExplain: This means divisions of the year.
These mean windy and windless conditions.
This means day-and-night.
Right: काल (time) + कृत (made).
questions.explain: कालकृताः opens the verse as the name of the class.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the conditions named.
questions.rule: These words come in the first half of the list.

questions.q: Put these periods of time in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The list runs: day-and-night, fortnight, month, season, half-year course.
questions.teaches: The periods of time in the list, in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which of these name a period of time, not light or weather?
optionExplain: Cold: a condition of weather.
Shade: a condition of light.
A month: a period.
A fortnight: a period.
questions.explain: Fortnight and month are periods; shade and cold are conditions.

questions.q: Which two words of the list mean cold and heat?
optionExplain: Right: शीत = cold, उष्ण = heat.
Sunshine and shade.
Moonlight and darkness.
Fortnight and month.
questions.explain: The verse joins the two as शीतोष्ण.

questions.q: By the sandhi in शीत + उष्ण = शीतोष्ण, what does शीत + उदक (cold water) give?
optionExplain: अ + उ does not give ऊ.
Right: अ + उ = ओ, as in शीतोष्ण.
अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
The two vowels do join here.
questions.explain: Short अ before उ joins as ओ.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: अ + उ joins into ओ.

questions.q: According to the text, how are these things causes of the four?
options: By the choice of the physician
By the passing of the seasons
optionExplain: The text says nature, not choice.
No such cause is named.
Right: स्वभावतः एव: by nature indeed.
No such cause is named.
questions.explain: स्वभावतः is the phrase: by their own nature.

questions.q: Match each of the four terms to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words of the compound.
questions.rule: Each is a member of the long compound in the verse.

questions.q: Put the four terms in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The verse reads: accumulation, aggravation, pacification, counteraction.
questions.teaches: The four terms of the compound, in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which word in the verse means of the doshas?
optionExplain: The plain plural, the doshas.
The locative, in the doshas.
The instrumental, by the doshas.
Right: Genitive plural: of the doshas.
questions.explain: दोषाणाम् is marked gen. pl. on the card.

questions.q: Which of these are among the four things the text names?
optionExplain: Taking up: not among the four terms.
Origin: not among the four terms.
Counteraction: the fourth term.
Aggravation: the second term.
questions.explain: Aggravation and counteraction are in the compound; origin and taking up are not.

questions.q: On the pattern of प्रयोजनवन्तः (having purpose), what does the invented word बलवन्तः mean?
optionExplain: Right: बल (strength) + वन्तः (having).
The ending does not negate.
The first member is strength, not purpose.
The ending does not mean of many.
questions.explain: -वन्तः after a noun means having that noun.
questions.teaches: -वन्तः after a noun makes a word meaning having that.

questions.q: Who is said to have declared this group to be the cause?
optionExplain: No kings speak in this verse.
Right: चिकित्सकैः: by physicians.
No students are named here.
No gods are named here.
questions.explain: The verse ends with चिकित्सकैः, by physicians.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: These are the base forms of words in the verse.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The verse runs: of bodily disorders, this group, in aggravation and pacification, cause declared, by physicians.
questions.teaches: The verse's phrases in order: the group is a cause in aggravation and pacification.

questions.q: In which two things does this verse call the group a cause?
optionExplain: These are in the previous unit, not here.
Neither is named.
Right: प्रकोपे प्रशमे च.
Neither is named.
questions.explain: The verse names the two: प्रकोप and प्रशम.
questions.rule: प्रकोपे प्रशमे च = in aggravation and in pacification.

questions.q: Which split is right for हेतुरुक्तः?
optionExplain: The र् belongs to the visarga, not to the next word.
The first word is हेतुः, not हेतोः.
The next word is उक्तः, which begins with a vowel.
Right: Visarga after -उ becomes र् before a vowel.
questions.explain: The card lists the words as हेतुः and उक्तः.

questions.q: On the pattern of चिकित्सकैः (by physicians), what does the invented word शिष्यैः mean?
optionExplain: Right: The ending -ऐः means by, plural.
Of would end in -आणाम्.
Among would end in -एषु.
To would be a singular ending.
questions.explain: शिष्य + ऐः = by students, as चिकित्सक + ऐः = by physicians.
questions.teaches: The instrumental plural ending -ऐः means by.

questions.q: In which two places does the verse say adventitious diseases fall?
options: In the skin and in the blood
In the mind and in the body
In the eyes and in the ears
In the home and in the field
optionExplain: Neither is named here.
Right: मनस्यन्ये शरीरेऽन्ये.
Neither is named here.
Neither is named here.
questions.explain: The verse says: some in the mind, others in the body.
questions.rule: मनसि = in the mind; शरीरे = in the body.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: मनसि and शरीरे are locatives; द्विधा is an indeclinable.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The verse runs: adventitious diseases, fall in two ways, some in the mind, others in the body, twofold treatment of them.
questions.teaches: The verse's phrases in order: two places, then a twofold treatment.

questions.q: Which word says that the treatment is twofold?
optionExplain: This says how the diseases fall: in two ways.
This is the verb: they fall.
Right: Marked f. nom. sg. and joined to क्रिया.
This only means of them.
questions.explain: द्विविधा agrees with क्रिया; द्विधा belongs to the falling.

questions.q: मनसि means in the mind. Which form means in the body?
optionExplain: This is the plain form, the body.
This means of the body.
This means by the body.
Right: A locative singular, in.
questions.explain: The verse uses शरीरे after मनसि.

questions.q: On the pattern of शरीरे (in the body), what does the invented word ग्रामे mean?
optionExplain: Right: A locative singular: in.
Of would end in -स्य.
From would end in -आत्.
By would end in -एण.
questions.explain: ग्राम + ए = in the village, as शरीर + ए = in the body.
questions.teaches: The locative singular ending -ए means in.

questions.q: What does the verse say brings comfort to the mental ones?
options: The group beginning with the elements
The desired group beginning with sound
Treatment like that of the bodily ones
optionExplain: That group is not mentioned here.
Right: शब्दादिरिष्टो वर्गः सुखावहः.
That is said of those fallen in the body.
That phrase is from the previous unit.
questions.explain: For the mental ones the verse names the desired group beginning with sound.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: Base forms of words in the verse.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The verse runs: for those fallen in the body, like the bodily; for the mental, the desired group of sound and the rest, comfort-bringing.
questions.teaches: The two halves of the verse, bodily then mental, in order.

questions.q: Which word means of the mental ones?
optionExplain: This means of the bodily ones.
This means of those fallen in the body.
Right: Genitive plural of मानस.
This means sound and the rest.
questions.explain: मानस means mental; -आनाम् is the genitive plural.

questions.q: What does -वत् in शारीरवत् mean on the card?
optionExplain: The card marks it as an indeclinable like-word.
From would end in -आत्.
Of would be a genitive form.
Right: The card marks शारीरवत् as indeclinable: like.
questions.explain: The word is indeclinable: like the bodily ones.

questions.q: By the sandhi in शब्द + आदि = शब्दादि, what does the invented रूप + आदि (form and the rest) give?
optionExplain: Right: अ + आ = आ, as in शब्दादि.
अ + आ does not give ए.
अ + आ does not give ओ.
The two vowels do join here.
questions.explain: Short अ before आ joins as long आ.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: अ + आ joins into long आ.

questions.q: Which four things does the text say were explained in brief?
options: Purusha, disease, medicinal substance, time of action
optionExplain: These are the groups of the earlier units.
Right: पुरुषो व्याधिरौषधं क्रियाकाल इति चतुष्टयम्.
These are parts named in an earlier unit.
These are the kinds of moving things.
questions.explain: The set is पुरुष, व्याधि, औषध and क्रियाकाल.

questions.q: Match each of these four mentions to what it covers.
pairs: substances he arises from, limbs, divisions
diseases from imbalance of vata, pitta, kapha, blood and their combination
procedures beginning with chedya and sneha
questions.explain: The first four mentions and what each brings in.
questions.rule: Each mention is followed by -ग्रहणात्: by the mention of.

questions.q: Put the five items listed under the mention of औषध in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The list runs: द्रव्य, रस, गुण, वीर्य, विपाक.
questions.teaches: The list given under the mention of औषध, in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which are named as the things whose imbalance causes the diseases?
optionExplain: A term listed under औषध, not under disease.
A term listed under औषध, not under disease.
Blood: named in the list.
Named first.
questions.explain: वात, पित्त, कफ and शोणित are the named things; द्रव्य and विपाक belong to औषध.

questions.q: In ओषधग्रहणात्, what does the ending -ग्रहणात् say?
optionExplain: The card gives mention, not taking up.
No purpose is stated.
Right: The card glosses it: by the mention of.
No genitive is meant.
questions.explain: -ग्रहणात् is ablative: by the mention of.

questions.q: On the pattern of व्याधिग्रहणात् (by the mention of disease), what does the invented वृक्षग्रहणात् mean?
options: In the mention of a tree
To the mention of a tree
optionExplain: That would be a plain nominative.
In would be a locative.
To would be another case.
Right: Same ablative -ग्रहणात्: by the mention of.
questions.explain: वृक्ष + ग्रहणात् = by the mention of tree.
questions.teaches: X-ग्रहणात् means by the mention of X.

questions.q: What is called the seed of therapeutics in this verse?
optionExplain: Right: बीजं चिकित्सितस्यैतत्समासेन प्रकीर्तितम्.
These are the exposition to come.
No students are named here.
No physician is named here.
questions.explain: एतत् points to what was just proclaimed in brief.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: These are words of the verse in their forms.

questions.q: This is the ____ (seed) of therapeutics. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: बीजम् is the word the verse uses for the seed.
questions.teaches: बीजम् = seed.
questions.rule: The brief statement is named the seed.

questions.q: Which word tells that the exposition lies in the future?
optionExplain: This tells of what is already proclaimed.
Right: A future verb: will be.
This tells how: in brief.
This is the genitive: of therapeutics.
questions.explain: भविष्यति is 3 sg. future of √भू: will be.
questions.rule: Future verb = what is yet to be.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The verse runs: the seed of therapeutics, this proclaimed in brief, hundred chapters with twenty, its exposition, will be.

questions.q: On the pattern of सविंशं शतम् (a hundred with twenty added), what does the invented सविंशं सहस्रम् mean?
options: A hundred with a thousand added
optionExplain: The units are not swapped.
सविंश does not multiply.
Right: सविंश + सहस्र: a thousand and twenty.
सविंश adds, not subtracts.
questions.explain: सविंश adds twenty to the number named.
questions.teaches: सविंशं शतम् = a hundred with twenty added; the same word added to another number adds twenty.

questions.q: What does the text say it does with the 120 chapters?
options: Reads them aloud to the students
Keeps them together in one book without any division
Divides them by subject matter into five sections
optionExplain: No reading aloud is stated.
The text says it divides them.
The text names five, not two.
Right: पञ्चसु स्थानेषु ... संविभज्य.
questions.explain: संविभज्य is having divided; पञ्चसु स्थानेषु is into five sections.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words and phrases of the line.
questions.rule: संविभज्य is an absolutive; व्याख्यास्यामः is a future verb.

questions.q: Put the five sections in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: The line runs: सूत्र, निदान, शारीर, चिकित्सित, कल्प.
questions.teaches: The five sections of the work, in the order of the text.

questions.q: Why does संविभज्य end in -य and not in -त्वा?
options: The root has the prefixes सम् and वि
The word is a verb in the future tense
The word is a noun in the plural number
The word is a noun in the locative case
optionExplain: Right: A prefixed root takes -य for having done.
-य does not mark the future.
-य does not mark the plural.
-य does not mark the locative.
questions.explain: The card lists √भज् with सम्-वि; prefixed roots take -य.

questions.q: Where does the text say the remaining topics will be explained?
options: In a sixth section added after Kalpa
optionExplain: The Sutra section is one of the five.
Right: उत्तरे तन्त्रे शेषानर्थान् व्याख्यास्यामः.
The Kalpa section is one of the five.
Only five sections are named.
questions.explain: The remaining topics go to the later treatise (उत्तरे तन्त्रे).
questions.rule: उत्तरे तन्त्रे = in the later treatise.

questions.q: On the pattern of संविभज्य (having divided), what does the invented संगृह्य mean?
optionExplain: A future verb would end in -ष्यामः or -स्यामः.
The ending -य is active, not passive.
Right: सम् + √ग्रह + -य: an absolutive.
The word is a verb form, not a noun.
questions.explain: A prefixed root with -य means having done.
questions.teaches: After a prefixed root, -य means having done it.

questions.q: Who is named as the one by whom this was spoken?
optionExplain: He is the one who made it known.
Kings honour the reader.
His world is the final reward.
Right: स्वयम्भुवा प्रोक्तम्.
questions.explain: स्वयम्भुवा is instrumental: by the Self-existent one.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: These are the verse's own words in their forms.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The verse runs: spoken by the Self-existent, made known by the lord of Kashi, he of meritorious deeds, honoured by kings on earth, at the end of life attains Shakra's world.
questions.teaches: The verse in order: who spoke it, who made it known, and what it states for the reader.

questions.q: By whom does the verse say the teaching was made known?
optionExplain: Right: काशिपतिप्रकाशितम्.
He is the one who spoke it.
Kings honour the reader.
No physicians appear in this verse.
questions.explain: प्रकाशितम् is made known; the doer is the lord of Kashi.
questions.rule: Speaker and publisher are different persons in the verse.

questions.q: Which does the verse state of the one who reads it?
options: He becomes the lord of Kashi
He is honoured by kings on earth
optionExplain: No commentary is mentioned.
That title belongs to the one who made it known.
भुवि पूजितो नृपैः.
पुण्यकर्मा.
questions.explain: The verse gives the reader merit, honour by kings and a result at the end of life.

questions.q: By the sandhi in नृपैः + असुक्षये = नृपैरसुक्षये, what does देवैः + अपि give?
optionExplain: The visarga does not simply vanish.
Right: Visarga after -ऐ before a vowel becomes र्.
The visarga joins to the next word.
The visarga does not become य्.
questions.explain: Visarga after a vowel other than अ or आ becomes र् before a vowel.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: a visarga after -ऐ before a vowel becomes र्.

questions.q: What do the speakers say they will do with the chapter?
optionExplain: No such verb appears in the line.
The form is future, not past.
Right: व्याख्यास्यामः means we shall expound.
The verb is expound, not listen.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः is the verb: we shall expound.

questions.q: Match each word of the opening to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four separate words once the joins are opened.
questions.rule: अथ and अतः are indeclinables; अध्यायम् is accusative; व्याख्यास्यामः is a future verb.

questions.q: We shall expound the Shishyopanayaniya ____ (chapter). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अध्यायम् is the accusative: the thing to be expounded.
questions.teaches: अध्यायम् = chapter, the object of the expounding.

questions.q: Which of these words are indeclinables (marked ind. on the card)?
optionExplain: A noun in the accusative.
ind.: now.
A verb form.
ind.: therefore.
questions.explain: The card marks अथ and अतः as ind.; the other two change with case or person.

questions.q: Put the words of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The line runs: now, therefore, concerning the initiation of the pupil, chapter, we shall expound.

questions.q: In the invented line वयं गमिष्यामः, what does गमिष्यामः mean?
optionExplain: Past would not use this ending.
They would need a third person ending.
This ending is plural, so not I.
Right: -ष्यामः is the same future ending as -स्यामः in व्याख्यास्यामः.
questions.explain: The ending -स्यामः / -ष्यामः is first person plural future.
questions.teaches: First person plural future: -स्यामः means we shall.

questions.q: Who is named in this unit as the one who said it?
optionExplain: Right: भगवान् धन्वन्तरिः is the subject of उवाच.
Only Dhanvantari is named here.
No pupil is named in this unit.
A speaker is named.
questions.explain: The unit names Dhanvantari as the speaker.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four words of the line once the join is opened.
questions.rule: यथा is an indeclinable; उवाच is the verb; भगवान् and धन्वन्तरिः are nominative.

questions.q: The revered one who said it is भगवान् ____. Type the name in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: The name stands in the nominative as the subject of उवाच.
questions.teaches: धन्वन्तरिः = Dhanvantari, the speaker.

questions.q: Which words are nominative singular (marked nom. sg. on the card)?
optionExplain: A verb: said.
m. nom. sg.: describes the speaker.
An indeclinable: as.
m. nom. sg.: the speaker's name.
questions.explain: Both भगवान् and धन्वन्तरिः are marked m. nom. sg.

questions.q: Put the words of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: As, said, the revered one, Dhanvantari.

questions.q: By the sandhi in यथा + उवाच = यथोवाच, what does तथा + उवाच give?
optionExplain: आ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
Right: आ + उ becomes ओ, as in यथोवाच.
The उ cannot simply vanish.
The two vowels do join in this sandhi.
questions.explain: आ + उ = ओ in sandhi, exactly as यथा + उवाच = यथोवाच.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: आ + उ joins into ओ.

questions.q: From which classes does the text say the pupil is taken?
options: Only from the sons of physicians.
Any one of the three classes.
All three classes together at once.
optionExplain: Three classes are named, not one.
No such limit is stated.
Right: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियवैश्यानाम् अन्यतमम्.
अन्यतमम् means any one of them.
questions.explain: The three classes are named and any one of them may be taken.

questions.q: Put these listed qualities in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: In the list the run is: strength, intelligence, steadfastness, memory, understanding.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the sentence.
questions.rule: भिषक् is nominative; शिष्यम् and अन्यतमम् are accusative; उपनयेत् is optative.
questions.teaches: Subject, object and optative verb of the sentence.

questions.q: Which words are accusative singular (marked acc. sg. on the card)?
optionExplain: m. nom. sg.: the physician, who acts.
m. acc. sg.: the pupil, object of the verb.
A verb: should initiate.
m. acc. sg.: any one.
questions.explain: The card marks शिष्यम् and अन्यतमम् as acc. sg.; the physician is nominative.

questions.q: A candidate is a vaishya and has all the qualities listed. What does the text allow?
options: He may not, as only brahmanas qualify.
He may not, as vaishyas are left out.
He may only if a brahmana is absent.
He may be taken; vaishyas are named.
optionExplain: Three classes are named, not one.
वैश्य is named in the text.
No such condition is stated.
Right: वैश्य is named in the list of three.
questions.explain: A vaishya with the listed qualities falls under the three classes named.
questions.rule: Read the list exactly as named.

questions.q: In the invented गुरुः शिष्यं पृच्छेत्, what does पृच्छेत् mean?
optionExplain: Right: -एत् is the optative ending, like उपनयेत्: should.
A past would not use -एत्.
A plain present would be पृच्छति.
That would be an absolutive.
questions.explain: -एत् gives the sense should or would.
questions.teaches: An optative ending gives the sense should or would.

questions.q: With what does the text say the square plot is smeared?
optionExplain: These are on the fuel sticks, not the plot.
Right: स्थण्डिलम् उपलिप्य गोमयेन.
Grass is spread over it, not smeared.
Ghee is for the oblations; water is sprinkled.
questions.explain: गोमयेन (with cow dung) goes with उपलिप्य (having smeared).

questions.q: Put these steps in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: Smearing, spreading, worshipping, drawing lines, placing the Brahman, kindling the fire.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the sentence.
questions.rule: गोमयेन and दर्भैः are instrumental; the first two describe the plot.
questions.teaches: Instrumentals and the measure words of the plot.

questions.q: Which words are absolutives (marked abs. on the card)?
optionExplain: An optative verb: should offer.
abs.: having smeared.
A causative optative: should cause to do.
abs.: having worshipped.
questions.explain: Both are marked abs.; the other two are optative verbs.

questions.q: What does the text say follows the ghee oblations?
options: The sprinkling of water on the plot.
The svaha utterance for each deity and the sages.
The worship of the deities with flowers.
optionExplain: That comes before the oblations.
That comes before the oblations.
Right: ततः ... स्वाहाकारं कुर्यात्.
That comes before the oblations.
questions.explain: After the oblations comes ततः, then the svaha utterance, and the pupil does it too.

questions.q: By the prefix pattern, which is the absolutive of आ + नी (to bring)?
optionExplain: -त्वा is used without a prefix.
That is a participle, not an absolutive.
That is a present verb.
Right: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य, as in उपलिप्य.
questions.explain: A prefixed verb takes -य, like उपलिप्य and संस्तीर्य.
questions.teaches: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य, not -त्वा.

questions.q: Whose initiation may a vaishya perform, according to the text?
optionExplain: Right: वैश्यो वैश्यस्यैव.
That is said of the brahmana.
That is said of the rajanya.
The text gives him a share.
questions.explain: वैश्यस्य एव means of a vaishya only.

questions.q: Put these persons in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: The brahmana, the rajanya, the vaishya, then the shudra.

questions.q: Match each person to what the text says of him.
pairs: some say: may be taught, not initiated, without mantras
questions.explain: Four statements of the unit.
questions.rule: त्रयाणाम्, द्वयस्य, वैश्यस्य एव fix the numbers; the shudra clause is a view of some.
questions.teaches: Who may initiate whom, and the view of some.

questions.q: Which statements agree with the unit?
options: A vaishya may initiate a brahmana.
A brahmana may initiate the three classes.
A rajanya may initiate all three classes.
A vaishya may initiate only a vaishya.
optionExplain: The text says only a vaishya.
त्रयाणां वर्णानाम्.
The text says of the two.
वैश्यस्य एव.
questions.explain: The numbers are three for the brahmana, two for the rajanya, one class for the vaishya.

questions.q: What do some say may be done for a shudra with family virtues?
options: He may be initiated, with all mantras.
He may be taught, uninitiated and without mantras.
He may be taught the mantras, not initiated.
He may not be taught at all.
optionExplain: The text says uninitiated.
Right: अनुपनीतम् अध्यापयेत् मन्त्रवर्जम्.
The text leaves the mantras out.
The view of some allows teaching.
questions.explain: The clause says: without mantras, uninitiated, he may be taught.

questions.q: In the invented ब्राह्मणः पठितुम् अर्हति, what does पठितुम् mean?
optionExplain: That would be an absolutive.
That would be a present verb.

-तुम् does not make a relative.
questions.explain: -तुम् is the infinitive: to do, to read.
questions.teaches: An infinitive in -तुम् with अर्हति says is entitled to do.

questions.q: With what as witness does the speaker address the pupil?

optionExplain: The deities were worshipped earlier, not named as witness.
The sages are not named as witness here.
The witness named is the fire.

questions.explain: अग्निसाक्षिकम् = having the fire as witness.

questions.q: Put these faults in the order in which the text names them.

questions.q: Match each fault to its meaning.
questions.explain: The first five faults of the list.
questions.rule: These are the first members of the series of faults to be abandoned.

questions.q: Which of these are named among the faults to be abandoned?

Laziness: in the list.
questions.explain: Truth, vows, celibacy and salutation are what the pupil is to be intent on.
questions.rule: Faults are given up (हित्वा); the other things are practised.

questions.q: Put the parts of the address in the order of the text.

Speaking to the pupil with the fire as witness
Abandoning desire, anger and the other faults
Being intent on truth, vows, celibacy and salutation
Acting in what is dear and beneficial to the speaker
If otherwise: unrighteousness and fruitless learning
questions.explain: Circling, address, faults abandoned, what to be intent on, conduct, the result of acting otherwise.

questions.q: In the invented शिष्येण पठितव्यम्, what is the sense?
optionExplain: Right: -तव्यम् says must, as in भवितव्यम्.
A past would not use -तव्यम्.
A present would be पठति.
-तव्यम् does not express wish.
questions.explain: -तव्यम् with the agent in the instrumental means must.
questions.teaches: A gerundive in -तव्यम् says what must be done.

questions.q: What two results does the speaker wish on himself?
options: Sharing in sin and fruitless learning.
optionExplain: Neither is mentioned here.
Right: एनोभाक् and अफलविद्यः.
Neither is mentioned here.
Neither is mentioned here.
questions.explain: The two results are a share in sin and learning that bears no fruit.
questions.rule: एनःभाक् = sharer in sin; अफलविद्यः = with fruitless learning.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the unit in the order of the text (one clause is left out).
questions.explain: I, while you conduct yourself rightly, may I become a sharer in sin, and one with fruitless learning.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the unit.
questions.rule: यदि opens the condition; एनोभाक् and अफलविद्यः name the results.
questions.teaches: The words of the condition and its results.

questions.q: Which words are optative, 1st person (marked 1 sg. opt.)?
optionExplain: A participle: behaving.
1 sg. opt.: I should be.
A pronoun: I.
1 sg. opt.: may I become.
questions.explain: The card marks both स्याम् and भवेयम् as 1 sg. opt.
questions.rule: 1st person optative: I should, may I.

questions.q: While the speaker wishes this on himself, what is said of the listener's conduct?

No leaving is mentioned.
Right: त्वयि सम्यग्वर्तमाने.
It stands in the first clause.

questions.q: In the invented यदि अहं गच्छेयम्, what does गच्छेयम् mean?
optionExplain: He would be गच्छेत्.
A past would not use -एयम्.
We would be गच्छेम.

questions.explain: -एयम् marks I should or may I.
questions.teaches: The ending -एयम् is the 1st person singular optative.

questions.q: For whom does the text say a remedy is not to be provided?
options: Brahmins, teachers, the poor and friends.
Friends, the poor and those treated like kinsmen.
optionExplain: Right: व्याधशाकुनिकपतितपापकारिणां न प्रतिकर्तव्यम्.
These are in the first group.
Both are in the first group.
These are in the first group.
questions.explain: The second group is of hunters, fowlers, the fallen and evildoers.
questions.rule: न प्रतिकर्तव्यम् = not to be provided.

questions.q: Put the gains in the order in which the text names them.

questions.q: Match each word of the first group to its meaning.

questions.q: For which of these does the text say a remedy is to be provided?

The fallen: in the second group.

questions.q: The text compares the care of the first group to what?

The honouring of the deities at a rite.

No king is mentioned.
No worship is mentioned.
questions.explain: इव means like: as for one's own kinsmen, and with one's own medicines.

questions.q: In the invented इदं छात्राणां पुस्तकम्, what does छात्राणाम् mean?
optionExplain: That would be instrumental, -ऐः.
That would be dative singular.

That would be locative, -एषु.
questions.explain: -आणाम् / -आनाम् is the genitive plural: of the many.

questions.q: What does this unit list, leaving its verb to the next unit?

No work is named here.

questions.q: Put these items of the unit in the order of the text (some items are left out).

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the unit.
questions.rule: कृष्णे and शुक्ले are locative singular; व्यथासु is locative plural.

questions.q: Which occasions are listed in this unit (not in the next)?

optionExplain: Not in this unit.

questions.q: In अकालविद्युत्स्तनयित्नुघोषे, what does the अ- of अकाल do?

optionExplain: Right: अ- before a consonant = not.
अ- does not strengthen.

questions.q: In the invented ग्रामेषु वसन्ति जनाः, what does ग्रामेषु mean?

questions.explain: -एषु / -आसु marks locative plural: in the many.

questions.q: What does the unit say an impure person is not to do?

questions.q: Which split of नाशुचिना is right?
optionExplain: ना is not a word here.

questions.q: Which occasions are named in this unit?

questions.q: In the invented अनृतं न वक्तव्यम्, what is the sense?
options: A falsehood should not be spoken.

A past would not use -तव्यम्.

questions.explain: न with a gerundive says should not be done.

questions.q: What do the speakers announce in this line?

That a pupil is being led to his teacher in the text.

questions.q: Which split of the joined word अथातः is right?

questions.q: Which description of व्याख्यास्यामः is right?
options: Third person plural future: they will expound.
First person plural past: we expounded.
First person singular future: I shall expound.
First person plural future: we shall expound.
optionExplain: The ending -स्यामः is first person.
The form is future, not past.
The ending is plural.

questions.q: By the same joining as अतः + अध्ययन = अतोऽध्ययन, what does पुरुषः + अयम् give?

The visarga does not simply vanish into आ.
-अः becomes ओ, not ए.

questions.q: What does this short unit give?
options: A list of titles from the work.
The name of the speaker whose words come next.
A reason for the name of a section.
A rule of conduct for the pupils.

Right: The unit holds only the speaker; the sentence goes on.
No such reason appears here.
No rule appears in this unit.

questions.q: Which words are in the nominative singular (the doer)?
optionExplain: An indeclinable: as.
A verb: said.
m. nom. sg.: the speaker's name.
m. nom. sg.: describes the speaker.

questions.q: Which split of the joined word यथोवाच is right?

The card gives यथा, with a long आ.

No word यथौ appears on the card.

optionExplain: आ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
The उ cannot simply vanish.
The two vowels do join in this sandhi.
Right: आ + उ becomes ओ, as in यथोवाच.
questions.explain: आ + उ = ओ, exactly as यथा + उवाच = यथोवाच.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: आ + उ joins into ओ.

questions.q: In how many sections does the unit say the earlier-stated chapters lie?
optionExplain: Right: पञ्चसु स्थानेषु = in five sections.
The text says five.
The text says five.
The text says five.

questions.q: How does the unit express the total of 120 chapters?
options: A hundred chapters with twenty taken away.
A hundred chapters with twenty added (सविंशम्).
A hundred chapters, of which twenty are lost.
Twenty groups of a hundred chapters each.
optionExplain: सविंशम् adds, it does not subtract.

Nothing is said of loss.
The sense is a hundred plus twenty.

questions.q: By the unit's counts, how many chapters do the Sutrasthana and the Chikitsitas have together?

questions.q: By the same स- pattern, what does the invented सपुत्रो राजा mean?
options: A king who is a son.

The compound describes the king, it does not name the son alone.
सपुत्र does not mean being a son.

questions.q: What does this verse give?
options: A list of chapter titles, beginning with the origin of the Veda.
A rule for choosing a teacher, in order.
A story of how the work was handed down.
A reason for the name of a section.
optionExplain: Right: वेदोत्पत्तिः opens the list.
No teacher or rule appears.
No story appears in the verse.
No such reason appears in this verse.

questions.q: Match each title to its meaning.

questions.q: Which of these titles does the card mark as feminine?

m. nom. sg.
m. nom. sg.

questions.q: Which split of the joined word वेदोत्पत्तिः is right?
optionExplain: The card gives वेद, ending in अ.
The card gives वेद, ending in अ.
Right: अ + उ joins into ओ.
औ before उ would not give ओ.
questions.explain: वेद + उत्पत्तिः joins as वेदोत्पत्तिः (अ + उ = ओ).

questions.q: By the same joining, what does ग्राम + उत्सवः give?
optionExplain: अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
The अ does not simply drop.
ए is the result of अ + इ.
Right: अ + उ becomes ओ, as in वेदोत्पत्तिः.

questions.teaches: Sandhi: अ + उ joins into ओ.

questions.q: Which of these is a chapter title in the verse?

questions.q: What does the dual अध्यायौ tell us about अग्निकर्म and जलौका?

They are three chapters in all.
They are the same chapter by two names.

The dual counts two.

questions.q: Which split of the joined word आख्यावध्यायौ is right?
optionExplain: The card gives the dual आख्यौ.
ऐ before अ would give आय्.
Right: औ before अ becomes आव्.
The card gives अध्यायौ, with its first अ.

questions.q: By the same joining, what does नौ + अयम् give?

questions.q: What is the subject of the title in the first line?

questions.q: What does the ending of दोषधातुमलाद्यानाम् show?

questions.q: In joining विज्ञान and अध्यायः, what do the two अ become?
