questions.rule: The first three are genitive singular; वारणः is a nominative.

questions.q: How are the three genitives पैत्तस्य, श्लैष्मिकस्य, रौधिरस्य filled out?
options: With a new subject, such as a physician.
With a verb of their own, such as to cure.
With nothing at all, as bare names in a list.
With abhishyanda, from the item before them.
optionExplain: No physician is named in this verse.
No verb is given for them.
A genitive needs a word it depends on.
Right: The note says abhishyanda is supplied.
questions.explain: Each is 'of such a kind', and the word supplied is abhishyanda, as in the first item.
questions.rule: A genitive list leans on a word named earlier.
questions.teaches: In a list, later genitives can depend on a word given once at the start.

questions.q: Which rendering lists the four kinds right?
options: Vata, Pitta, Kapha and the blood kind.
Vata, Pitta, Kapha and the ear kind.
Vata, Pitta, Kapha and the sweat kind.
Vata, Pitta, Kapha and the bone kind.
optionExplain: Right: वात, पैत्त, श्लैष्मिक, रौधिर.
रौधिरस्य is of blood, not of the ear.
No sweat is named in the verse.
रौधिरस्य is of blood, not of bone.
questions.explain: The fourth kind is the blood kind, रौधिर, from रुधिर (blood).

questions.q: Put the four kinds of abhishyanda in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse gives Vata first, then the Pitta, Kapha and blood kinds.

questions.q: In the invented compound अग्निवारणः, what does it mean?
optionExplain: In वाताभिष्यन्दवारणः the first member is warded off, not warding.
Right: Like वाताभिष्यन्दवारणः (warding off of Vata flux): the first member names what is warded off.
There is no ward in this compound.
वारण is warding off, not kindling.
questions.explain: In X-वारणः, X is what is warded off.
questions.teaches: In a compound ending in वारण, the first member names what is warded off.

questions.q: Which item of the second line arises in the ear?
optionExplain: That is the course of procedure.
That is injury.
Right: कर्ण-उत्थाः: those arising in the ear.
That is treatment.
questions.explain: कर्ण is the ear and उत्थाः means arising.

questions.q: Match each word of the second line to its meaning.
questions.explain: The four items of the second line.
questions.rule: Each of them stands in the nominative.

questions.q: Those arising in the ____ (ear). Type the word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: कर्ण is the first member of कर्णोत्थाः.
questions.teaches: कर्ण = ear.
questions.rule: In a compound the first member names the place.

questions.q: Which split of तच्चिकित्सितम् is right?
optionExplain: म् before च gives a nasal (तञ्चिकित्सितम्), not च्च.
No word ends in तच् here.
ततः before च would give ततश्च.
Right: त् before च joins as च्च.
questions.explain: तत् means their; त् before च becomes च्, which joins into च्च.

questions.q: Put the four items of the second line in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The line gives the course of procedure, injury, those arising in the ear, then their treatment.

questions.q: By the sandhi in तच्चिकित्सितम्, what does तत् + चरितम् join into?
optionExplain: Right: त् + च = च्च, as in तच्चिकित्सितम्.
The two are joined, and त् changes.
द् and a new अ do not appear.
The final त् does not turn into त.
questions.explain: Final त् before च turns into च्, so तत् + चरितम् is तच्चरितम्.
questions.teaches: Final त् before च joins as च्च.

questions.q: Which part of the body is named in घ्राणोत्थानाम्?
optionExplain: The ear is in the previous unit.
Right: घ्राण is the nose.
The head is named by शिरः, later in the unit.
The eyelid is in an earlier unit.
questions.explain: घ्राण-उत्थानाम् means of those arising in the nose.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the unit.
questions.rule: Each of the last three names a kind of act; the first names a part of the body.

questions.q: The discrimination of ____ diseases. Type the word for head in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: शिरः is the head; before गद it joins as शिरो.
questions.teaches: शिरः = head.
questions.rule: In a compound the first member names where the disease lies.

questions.q: Which rendering of the second line is right?
options: The treatment of pratishyaya and the discrimination of head diseases.
The checking of head diseases and the discrimination of pratishyaya.
The checking of pratishyaya and the discrimination of head diseases.
The recognition of pratishyaya and the checking of head diseases.
optionExplain: The word is निषेधः, checking, not treatment.
The two objects are swapped.
Right: प्रतिश्यायनिषेधः and शिरोगदविवेचनम् in that order.
Recognition belongs to the first line.
questions.explain: The line has checking for pratishyaya and discrimination for head diseases.

questions.q: Put the four items of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Recognition, then counteracting their diseases, then the checking of pratishyaya, then head diseases.

questions.q: By the sandhi in शिरोगद, what does तपः + वनम् join into?
optionExplain: The visarga is not kept before a voiced sound.
The visarga after अ does not give ए.
The visarga does not simply drop here.
Right: अः before a voiced sound becomes ओ, as शिरः + गद.
questions.explain: अः before a voiced letter (here व) turns into ओ.
questions.teaches: Visarga after अ, before a voiced sound, becomes ओ (शिरः + गद gives शिरोगद).

questions.q: What name does the verse give to the treatment of their diseases?
optionExplain: Right: शालाक्यं तन्त्रमुच्यते: it is called Shalakya.
The name in this unit is Shalakya.
That name is not given here.
That name is not given here.
questions.explain: The first line calls the treatment of their diseases the Shalakya tantra.
questions.rule: शालाक्यं तन्त्रम् उच्यते = is called the Shalakya tantra.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words from the second line.
questions.rule: नव-ग्रह-आकृति-ज्ञानम् is one compound: knowledge of the forms of the nine seizers.

questions.q: The knowledge of the forms of the nine ____ (seizers). Type the word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: ग्रह is the second member of नवग्रहाकृतिज्ञानम्.
questions.teaches: ग्रह = seizer.
questions.rule: The second member of the compound names whose forms are known.

questions.q: Which split of तन्त्रमुच्यते is right?
optionExplain: मुच्यते would be another verb, is released.
Right: म् joins with the following उ as मु.
च्यते is not a word.
A visarga would not give म.
questions.explain: तन्त्रम् is the noun and उच्यते the verb, is called.
questions.rule: म् + स्वर joins as the consonant म with that vowel.

questions.q: Put these parts of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The treatment, the name Shalakya, the knowledge of the nine seizers, the checking of Skanda.

questions.q: In the invented phrase तद्गुणानां ज्ञानम्, what does तद्गुणानाम् mean?
optionExplain: The ending -आनाम् is plural, not singular.
By would be तद्गुणैः.
Right: तद्- at the head means their, as in तद्गदानाम् (of their diseases).
From would be तद्गुणेभ्यः.
questions.explain: तद्गुणानाम् is genitive plural, like तद्गदानाम्: of their qualities.
questions.teaches: तद्- at the head of a compound means their or those; -आनाम् is genitive plural.

questions.q: Which two names are joined in the compound अपस्मारशकुन्योः?
optionExplain: Revati stands on its own after च.
Putana comes in the second line.
They are separate words in the verse.
Right: अपस्मार-शकुन्योः: of the two, Apasmara and Shakuni.
questions.explain: The first compound pairs Apasmara with Shakuni.

questions.q: Match each word of the first line to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the first line.
questions.rule: च, पुनः, पृथक् are indeclinables; रेवत्याः is genitive singular.

questions.q: What does the ending of शकुन्योः show?
options: Two names taken together: of the two.
One name only, taken alone: of it.
Many names in a row: of them all.
A place where it stands: in the two.
optionExplain: Right: The card marks it as a dvandva in the dual.
A single name would end in -ः or -स्य.
Many would use a plural ending.
The card marks it as genitive, not as place.
questions.explain: The card says dvandva, genitive dual: of the two names together.
questions.teaches: A dvandva compound with -योः names two things together: of the two.

questions.q: Which rendering of the first line is right?
options: Of Apasmara and Shakuni, and again together of Revati.
Of Apasmara and Shakuni, and again separately of Revati.
Of Apasmara and Shakuni, and never separately of Revati.
Of Apasmara and Revati, and again separately of Shakuni.
optionExplain: पृथक् is separately, not together.
Right: The line says again and separately.
पुनः is again, not never.
Shakuni is joined with Apasmara.
questions.explain: The first line pairs the first two names and then takes Revati again, separately.

questions.q: Put these five names in the order in which the unit gives them (one name is left out).
questions.explain: The unit goes from the pair to Revati, Putana, Mandika and Shitaputana.

questions.q: In the invented compound गुरुशिष्ययोः, what does it mean?
options: Of the teacher and the students.
By the teacher and the student.
Of the teacher and the student.
optionExplain: The ending -योः is dual, not plural.
By would be गुरुशिष्याभ्याम्.
Right: Like शकुन्योः: a dual dvandva, of the two.
A dvandva pairs two things, no teacher-of.
questions.explain: A dvandva with -योः names two: the teacher and the student, of the two.
questions.teaches: A dvandva in the dual genitive means 'of the two' joined: गुरुशिष्ययोः is of the teacher and the student.

questions.q: What name does the unit give to this group?
optionExplain: That name is in an earlier unit.
That name is for the Tantra beyond the chapters.
That name comes in a later unit.
Right: कौमारतन्त्रम् इति एतत् कीर्तितम्: this is declared the Kaumara tantra.
questions.explain: The second line says this is declared the Kaumara tantra.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the unit.
questions.rule: चिकित्सा is a feminine nominative; कीर्तितम् is a past participle.

questions.q: The ____ (origin) of the seizers. Type the word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: उत्पत्तिः is the second member of ग्रहोत्पत्तिः.
questions.teaches: उत्पत्ति = origin.
questions.rule: The second member of the compound names what is stated of the seizers.

questions.q: What does the text state about Naigamesha?
optionExplain: Right: नैगमेशचिकित्सा: the treatment of Naigamesha.
The origin is stated of the seizers.
No knowledge is named here.
No checking is named here.
questions.explain: The compound नैगमेश-चिकित्सा means the treatment of Naigamesha.

questions.q: Put these items in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Treatment of Naigamesha, origin of the seizers, the Kaumara tantra, declared.

questions.q: By the sandhi in ग्रहोत्पत्तिः, what does सूर्य + उदयः join into?
optionExplain: The two vowels join in this sandhi.
Right: अ + उ = ओ, as ग्रह + उत्पत्तिः gives ग्रहोत्पत्तिः.
अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
The two vowels do not merge into ऊ.
questions.explain: अ + उ = ओ.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: a short अ before उ joins to ओ.

questions.q: What three names does ज्वरातिसारशोषाणाम् join?
optionExplain: Thirst and cough come in the next unit.
Fainting is a separate name in this unit.
Right: ज्वर, अतिसार, शोष.
Vomiting comes in the next unit.
questions.explain: The first compound holds fever, purging and wasting.
questions.rule: ज्वर = fever; अतिसार = purging; शोष = wasting.

questions.q: Match each name to its literal meaning.
questions.explain: Five names of the unit with the card's literal glosses.
questions.rule: These are names only; the card gives plain literal meanings.

questions.q: What do the genitive endings in पाण्डूनाम्, रक्तपित्तस्य, मूर्च्छायाः show?
options: Each is a doer, one acting on its own.
Each is a place, standing for the word in.
Each is a verb, standing for the word is.
Each is 'of such', leaning on a word given later.
optionExplain: A genitive is not the doer.
Place would be the locative.
These are nouns with case endings.
Right: The card says the list continues into the next unit.
questions.explain: These are genitives of a list; the words they depend on come in the next unit.
questions.rule: A genitive says of; it leans on another word.
questions.teaches: A run of genitives in a list depends on a governing word that may come later.

questions.q: Which of these names does this unit list?
optionExplain: Listed in the first compound.
Not here; thirst is in the next unit.
Listed as fainting.
Not here; breathlessness is in the next unit.
Listed as blood-pitta.
questions.explain: Fever, fainting and blood-pitta are in this unit; thirst and breathlessness come next.
questions.rule: Only the names of the unit count.

questions.q: Put these names in the order in which the unit lists them.
questions.explain: The unit moves from the first compound to gulma and heart-affliction, pandu, raktapitta and fainting.

questions.q: In the invented word आम्रपनसजम्बूनाम्, what does it mean?
optionExplain: Right: One ending -नाम् at the end covers all the members.
The ending covers every member of the compound.
Jambu is also a member.
From would be -एभ्यः.
questions.explain: In a dvandva only the last member carries the ending, and it covers all.
questions.rule: Dvandva: one ending for all members.
questions.teaches: In a dvandva list one case ending, on the last member, belongs to every member.

questions.q: What does the second line state for स्वरभेद?
optionExplain: Checking is stated in the first line, for others.
Right: स्वरभेदचिकित्सा: the treatment of voice-break.
No recognition is named in this unit.
No origin is named in this unit.
questions.explain: The second line begins with स्वरभेदचिकित्सा, treatment of voice-break.

questions.q: Match each name to its literal meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the first line.

questions.q: The checking of ____ (thirst). Type the word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: तृष्णायाः is genitive singular of तृष्णा.
questions.teaches: तृष्णा = thirst.
questions.rule: The genitive gives what the checking is of.

questions.q: For which items does the verse state checking (निषेधः)?
optionExplain: No: for voice-break the text states treatment.
Yes: the checking of thirst.
Yes: the checking of hiccup.
No: the nose is not named in this unit.
Yes: and of breathlessness.
questions.explain: The first line gives checking for thirst, vomiting, hiccup, breathlessness and cough.
questions.rule: निषेधः governs the genitives of the first line.

questions.q: Put these items in the order in which the unit gives them.
questions.explain: Thirst, vomiting and hiccup, breathlessness and cough, then treatment of voice-break.

questions.q: By the sandhi in तृष्णायाश्छ, what does रामः + च join into?
optionExplain: ो comes before a voiced sound, and च is not voiced.
ः before च does not become स्.
Right: ः before च becomes श्, as ः before छ does in तृष्णायाश्छ.
The visarga does not stay before च.
questions.explain: Visarga before a palatal (च, छ) changes to श्.
questions.teaches: Visarga before च or छ becomes श् (तृष्णायाः + छ gives तृष्णायाश्छ).

questions.q: What does the verse say is set out here?
optionExplain: शेषम् is the remainder, not the whole.
शेषम् points to what is left, not the start.
The verse says body-treatment, not surgery.
Right: कायचिकित्सायाः शेषम् अत्र प्रकीर्तितम्.
questions.explain: The second line says the remainder of the body-treatment is set out here.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the unit.
questions.rule: The first two are names; the last two are ordinary words.

questions.q: The ____ (remainder) of the body-treatment is set out here. Type the word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: शेषम् is the subject of प्रकीर्तितम्.
questions.teaches: शेष = remainder.
questions.rule: The subject of a passive participle stands in the nominative.

questions.q: Which rendering of the second line is right?
options: Thus the remainder of the body-treatment is set out here.
Thus the remainder of the body-treatment is set out elsewhere.
Thus the whole of the body-treatment is set out here.
Thus the remainder of the body-treatment is hidden here.
optionExplain: Right: इति, शेषम्, अत्र, प्रकीर्तितम् in order.
अत्र is here, not elsewhere.
शेषम् is the remainder.
प्रकीर्तितम् is set out, not hidden.
questions.explain: Each word of the line fixes one part: thus, remainder, here, set out.

questions.q: Put these parts of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The pair of names comes first, then thus, the body-treatment, the remainder, here, set out.

questions.q: By the -त्र ending of अत्र (here), what does अन्यत्र mean?
optionExplain: Time words do not use -त्र.
Right: अन्य (other) + -त्र (in a place), as अत्र is here.
Otherwise would be अन्यथा.
Always would be सदा.
questions.explain: -त्र makes a place word: अत्र here, so अन्यत्र is in another place.
questions.teaches: The ending -त्र makes place words: अत्र (here), अन्यत्र (elsewhere).

questions.q: What is the group in this unit declared to be?
optionExplain: That name belongs to an earlier group.
That name belongs to an earlier group.
Right: भूतविद्या निरुच्यते: it is declared Bhutavidya.
That name is for the Tantra beyond the chapters.
questions.explain: The last words say the group is declared Bhutavidya.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the unit.
questions.rule: अमानुष is from अ- and मानुष; निरुच्यते is a passive verb.

questions.q: In भूतविद्या निरुच्यते, what is the role of भूतविद्या?
options: It is the one declaring, that is the speaker.
It is the place where it is declared, the locale.
It is the time when it is declared, the moment.
It is what is declared, not the one declaring.
optionExplain: A passive verb has no such doer here.
Place would take the locative.
Time would take another ending.
Right: निरुच्यते is passive: is declared.
questions.explain: In the passive, the nominative names what is acted on.
questions.rule: Passive: the nominative is what is acted on.
questions.teaches: With a passive verb (-यते), the subject is what is acted on: भूतविद्या is declared.

questions.q: Which rendering of the two named checkings and the closing name is right?
options: The checking of non-human beings and of unmada: this is declared Bhutavidya.
The recognition of non-human beings and of unmada: this is declared Bhutavidya.
The checking of non-human beings and of unmada: this is declared Shalakya.
The checking of human beings and of unmada: this is declared Bhutavidya.
optionExplain: Right: The unit gives these checkings and ends with the name.
The word is निषेधः, checking, not recognition.
The name stated is Bhutavidya.
अमानुष is non-human, not human.
questions.explain: Only one rendering keeps checking, non-human and the name Bhutavidya.
questions.rule: अमानुषनिषेधः and उन्मादप्रतिषेधः end in भूतविद्या निरुच्यते.

questions.q: Put these parts of the unit in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Checking of non-human beings, checking of unmada, the name Bhutavidya, then is declared.

questions.q: By the अ- of अमानुष, what does अदृष्टम् mean?
optionExplain: अ- does not strengthen.
Right: अ- + दृष्टम् (seen), as अ- + मानुष is non-human.
अ- does not repeat.
अ- does not mean first.
questions.explain: अ- before a consonant says not.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- before a consonant negates the word: अदृष्टम् is not seen.

questions.q: What does the verse call these chapters?
optionExplain: तन्त्रभूषणाः is ornaments, not roots.
No limbs are named in this verse.
Right: तन्त्रभूषणाः: ornaments of the treatise.
No students are named in this verse.
questions.explain: The last word is तन्त्रभूषणाः, the ornaments of the treatise.

questions.q: Match each term to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four terms of the verse.
questions.rule: भेदाः means varieties; वृत्तिः means regimen; भूषणाः means ornaments.

questions.q: The ____ (varieties) of rasa and dosha. Type the word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: भेदाः is the second member of रसभेदाः and दोषभेदाः.
questions.teaches: भेद = variety.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse list?
optionExplain: Not in this verse; it is in the previous unit.
Listed: varieties of rasa.
Not in this verse; it is in an earlier unit.
Listed: regimen of the healthy.
Listed: varieties of dosha.
questions.explain: The verse lists rasa varieties, the regimen of the healthy, the devices and dosha varieties.
questions.rule: Only the verse's own items count.

questions.q: Put these terms in the order in which the verse gives them.
questions.explain: The verse lists rasa, the regimen, the devices, dosha, and ends with the ornaments.

questions.q: By the compound तन्त्रभूषणाः, what does the invented नगरभूषणम् mean?
options: The city made by an ornament.
optionExplain: In would need a locative ending.
The first member is owner, not maker.
नगर is singular, and for needs another case.
Right: Like तन्त्र-भूषणाः: the first member is whose ornament.
questions.explain: X-भूषण = the ornament of X.
questions.teaches: In X-भूषण, the first member is the one adorned: the ornament of X.

questions.q: Which reason for the name Uttara does the verse give first?
optionExplain: Right: श्रेष्ठत्वात् is the first reason in the verse.
No length is mentioned.
The verse says last, not middle.
The verse says many topics.
questions.explain: The first reason is श्रेष्ठत्वात्, because of excellence.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are five words of the verse once the joins are opened.
questions.rule: The two -आत् words are ablative singular and give reasons.

questions.q: Which word carries the second sense of Uttara, the sense of last?
optionExplain: It means best, the first sense.
Right: It is glossed last, and stands beside उत्तरम्.
It means from gathering, a reason.
It means treatise, the thing named.
questions.explain: पश्चिमम् is the word for last; श्रेष्ठम् is the word for best.
questions.rule: Uttara is used in two senses.
questions.teaches: Uttara can mean higher or best, and also later or last; the verse uses both.

questions.q: Which of these does the verse say of the Uttara?
optionExplain: No length is mentioned.
The second half says it is best.
The verse says last, not first.
The second half ends with last.
बह्वर्थसंग्रहात् gives this as a reason.
questions.explain: The verse calls it best and last, and gives gathering many topics as a reason.

questions.q: Put these words and phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: First because of excellence, then the sages call, then because it gathers many topics, then best, then last.

questions.q: By the pattern of श्रेष्ठत्वात्, what does the invented वीरत्वात् mean?
optionExplain: -आत् does not mean in spite of.
-आत् does not mean towards.
Right: -त्व makes a state (heroism) and -आत् gives the reason.
With would be a different case ending.
questions.explain: वीर + त्व + आत् = because of heroism, like श्रेष्ठ + त्व + आत्.
questions.rule: -त्व states a quality; -आत् gives the reason.
questions.teaches: -त्व makes a noun of state (excellence, heroism) and the ablative -आत् says because of it.

questions.q: Which treatise holds the four named in the verse?
optionExplain: Shalakya is one of the four, not the holder.
Kaumara is one of the four, not the holder.
Bhutavidya is one of the four, not the holder.
Right: उत्तरसंज्ञिते says named Uttara.
questions.explain: The four are in the treatise named Uttara.
questions.rule: तन्त्रे उत्तरसंज्ञिते = in the treatise named Uttara.

questions.q: Put the four items in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The verse runs: Shalakya, Kaumara, the body-treatment, Bhutavidya.

questions.q: The verse says ____ (four, neuter) items are in the treatise named Uttara. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: चत्वारि is the neuter nominative plural of four, closing the list.
questions.teaches: चत्वारि = four.
questions.rule: A number closes the list and tells how many items stand in it.

questions.q: Which of these are named among the four in this verse?
optionExplain: Not named in this verse.
Named first in the verse.
Not named in this verse.
Named second in the verse.
questions.explain: Only Shalakya and Kaumara of these four options are named here.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse; the last two form the third item.
questions.rule: तन्त्रे is locative singular; उत्तरसंज्ञिते agrees with it.

questions.q: Joining तु and उत्तर gives तूत्तर. What does मधु + उक्तम् give by the same rule?
optionExplain: Right: उ + उ join into ऊ, as in तूत्तर.
उ + उ does not give ओ.
उ before a like vowel does not turn into व्.
The two vowels do join, they do not stay as one short उ.
questions.explain: Like vowels join into one long vowel: उ + उ = ऊ.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: two like vowels join into the long vowel, उ + उ = ऊ.

questions.q: Which item in the verse is called a poison treatise?
optionExplain: This is the rasayana procedure.
Right: विष means poison and तन्त्रम् means treatise.
This is knowledge of shalya.
This word means completely and is not an item.
questions.explain: विषतन्त्रम् is the poison treatise.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: तथा and पुनः are indeclinables; the other three are nouns.

questions.q: What kind of compound is रसायनविधिः, rasayana procedure?
options: A compound where both words are equal and joined.
A compound meaning one who has a procedure.
A compound where the first word stands in a case relation to the second.
A compound with a number as its first word.
optionExplain: That would be a joined pair, not marked here.
That would be a bahuvrihi, not marked here.
Right: The card marks it tat-purusha: procedure of rasayana.
रसायन is not a number.
questions.explain: The card marks रसायनविधिः as tat-purusha.
questions.rule: Tat-purusha: the first member stands in a case relation to the second.
questions.teaches: In a tat-purusha the first word stands in a case relation to the second, here rasayana-vidhi, the procedure of rasayana.

questions.q: Which of these words are nouns in the nominative singular on the card?
optionExplain: An indeclinable.
m. nom. sg.
An indeclinable.
n. nom. sg.
n. nom. sg.
questions.explain: The three items are nominative singular; तथा and पुनः are indeclinables.
questions.rule: Nominative singular names the listed item.

questions.q: Put these words in the order in which they stand in the verse (other words stand between them).
questions.explain: The verse gives the rasayana procedure, likewise, the poison treatise, further, knowledge of shalya.

questions.q: By the pattern of रसायनविधिः, what does the invented पठनविधिः mean?
optionExplain: That would be a bahuvrihi, not this pattern.
The first word relates to the second, they are not a pair.
Nothing here means without.
Right: पठन (reading) + विधि (procedure), like रसायन + विधि.
questions.explain: पठनविधिः is the procedure of reading.
questions.rule: Tat-purusha: first word stands in a case relation to the second.
questions.teaches: A tat-purusha names a thing by relating two nouns: X-विधिः = the procedure of X.

questions.q: What do those who study it by rule and apply it become?
optionExplain: Right: भवन्ति प्राणदा भुवि says exactly this.
No kingship is mentioned.
No mastery over sages is mentioned.
That belongs to another verse.
questions.explain: They become givers of life on earth.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: विधिना is instrumental singular; प्राणदाः is nominative plural.

questions.q: The treatise is ____ (of eight limbs). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अष्टाङ्गम् joins अष्ट (eight) and अङ्ग (limb) in a bahuvrihi: having eight limbs.
questions.teaches: अष्ट + अङ्ग = having eight limbs.
questions.rule: A bahuvrihi describes something by what it has.

questions.q: Which translation of the verse is right?
options: Thus this treatise of six limbs was revealed by the primal god; those who study and apply it by rule become givers of life on earth.
Thus this treatise of eight limbs was revealed by the primal god; those who study and apply it by rule become givers of life on earth.
Thus this treatise of eight limbs was revealed by a king; those who study and apply it by rule become givers of life on earth.
Thus this treatise of eight limbs was revealed by the primal god; those who study and apply it by rule become givers of life in heaven.
optionExplain: The verse says eight limbs, not six.
Right: Every word agrees with the verse.
The verse says the primal god, not a king.
The verse says on earth, not in heaven.
questions.explain: Only the first translation changes nothing in the verse.
questions.rule: Check each noun against the verse.

questions.q: Put these parts of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Thus eight limbs, this treatise, revealed by the primal god, by rule, applying, they become givers of life on earth.

questions.q: By the pattern of प्राणदाः, what does the invented ज्ञानदः गुरुः mean?
options: A teacher who is a receiver of knowledge.
A teacher who is a giver of knowledge.
optionExplain: -द gives; it does not receive.
Nothing here means without.
Right: -द at the end of a compound means giver, as in प्राणदाः.
The word is a compound, not a genitive.
questions.explain: ज्ञानद is giver of knowledge, like प्राणद, giver of life.
questions.rule: -द at the end of a compound = giver.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -द names a giver: प्राणद, giver of life; ज्ञानद, giver of knowledge.

questions.q: Whom does the text call worthy of a king?
options: A physician who serves a king.
optionExplain: No one is called worthy for studying once.
Students are not mentioned.
Serving a king is not mentioned.
Right: उभयज्ञो हि भिषक् राजार्हो भवति.
questions.explain: The knower of both is called worthy of a king.

questions.q: Match each word of the passage to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the passage.
questions.rule: The first two are gerundives; the other three name the physician, the knower and his worth.

questions.q: The practical work must also be pursued ____ (necessarily). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अवश्यम् stands twice in the passage: once for studying, once for the practical work.
questions.teaches: अवश्यम् = necessarily.
questions.rule: अवश्यम् strengthens a gerundive into a must.

questions.q: Which two words are gerundives, meaning to be done?
optionExplain: An absolutive: having studied.
gerundive: to be studied.
A noun: physician.
gerundive: to be practised.
questions.explain: The card marks अध्येयम् and उपासितव्यम् as gerundives; अधीत्य is an absolutive.

questions.q: Put these parts of the passage in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Must be studied, having studied, the work too must be pursued, the knower of both is a physician, worthy of a king he becomes.

questions.q: In the invented line पाठः पठितव्यः, what does पठितव्यः mean?
optionExplain: Right: -तव्य makes a gerundive, as in उपासितव्यम्.
That would be an absolutive such as अधीत्य.
-तव्य is not a past ending.
Nothing here means cannot.
questions.explain: पठितव्यः is the gerundive of read: to be read.
questions.teaches: -तव्य added to a root gives to be done: उपासितव्यम्, पठितव्यः.

questions.q: To whom does the verse compare such a man?
options: A timid man reaching a battle.
optionExplain: No hunter is mentioned.
Right: भीरुरिवाहवम् says this.
No teacher is mentioned.
No guest is mentioned.
questions.explain: The comparison is a timid man reaching a battle.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: अपरिनिष्ठितः and केवलशास्त्रज्ञः describe the man; मुह्यति is the verb.

questions.q: What does अपरिनिष्ठितः say of the man's work?
optionExplain: अ- negates; it does not strengthen.
Nothing here means new.
Right: अ- negates परिनिष्ठित, well versed.
Nothing here means by others.
questions.explain: अ- before the participle makes not well versed.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- negates the word after it: अपरिनिष्ठित = not well versed.

questions.q: In what is the man not well versed, according to the verse?
optionExplain: He knows the treatise, केवलशास्त्रज्ञः.
Kings are not mentioned.
Reading aloud is not mentioned.
Right: कर्मसु अपरिनिष्ठितः.
questions.explain: He knows only the treatise; he is not well versed in practical work.

questions.q: Put these parts of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Who knows only the treatise, not well versed in work, he is bewildered, on reaching a patient, like a timid man a battle.

questions.q: Which word completes the invented line यः कर्म करोति, ____ फलं लभते?
optionExplain: Right: सः is the correlative of यः, both masculine singular nominative.
तम् is accusative; the doer needs the nominative.
ते is plural; यः is singular.
ताः is feminine plural.
questions.explain: यः (who) is answered by सः (he).
questions.teaches: यः (who) is answered by सः (he), matching in gender, number and case.

questions.q: How does the verse describe this man's relation to the treatise?
options: Far advanced in it through effort.
Cast out from it through audacity.
Taught by it at the court.
optionExplain: The verse says cast out, not advanced.
Right: धार्ष्ट्याच्छास्त्रबहिष्कृतः says this.
No court is mentioned.
The verse says cast out, not admitted.
questions.explain: He is cast out from the treatise through audacity.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: धार्ष्ट्यात् is ablative; सत्सु is locative plural.

questions.q: He does not obtain ____ (honour) among the good. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: पूजाम् is the accusative, the object of नाप्नोति.
questions.teaches: पूजाम् = honour, the thing not obtained.
questions.rule: The accusative -म् marks the object of a verb.

questions.q: What does the verse say he does not get, and what does it say he deserves?
options: Honour among the good; death at the king's hands.
No honour among the good; a gift from the king.
No honour among the good; death at the king's hands.
Honour from the king; death among the good.
optionExplain: The verse says he does not win honour.
The verse says वध, death, not a gift.
Right: पूजां नाप्नोति and वधं चार्हति राजतः.
The places are swapped.
questions.explain: He wins no honour among the good and deserves death from the king.

questions.q: Put these parts of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Who is skilled in work, cast out through audacity, he among the good, honour does not win, and deserves death from the king.

questions.q: By the pattern of धार्ष्ट्यात्, what does भयात् mean in the invented line भयात् सः पलायते?
optionExplain: In would be a locative ending.
For the sake of would be a dative idea.
With would be an instrumental idea.
Right: The ablative -आत् gives the cause, as in धार्ष्ट्यात्.
questions.explain: भयात् = out of fear; he flees out of fear.
questions.teaches: The ablative can give the cause: धार्ष्ट्यात्, through audacity; भयात्, out of fear.

questions.q: In the comparison, what is said of the wings of the two birds?
optionExplain: Right: एकपक्षौ means one-winged.
The verse says one-winged.
No such number is mentioned.
The verse says one wing.
questions.explain: The two are like birds with one wing each.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: The first four are masculine dual; स्वकर्मणि is locative singular.

questions.q: The words उभौ and एतौ end in -औ. What number do they show here?
optionExplain: The card does not mark them singular.
Right: The card marks both m. nom. du.
The card does not mark them plural.
The card gives them case and number.
questions.explain: Both are marked masculine nominative dual.
questions.rule: -औ can be dual nominative; check the card.
questions.teaches: In this verse -औ is the masculine nominative dual ending; -औ is not always dual, so check the grammar label.

questions.q: Which of these are said of the two in the first line of the verse?
optionExplain: This stands in the second line.
अनिपुणौ stands in the first line.
This stands in the second line.
असमर्थौ stands in the first line.
questions.explain: Unskilled and unable are in the first line; half the Veda and one-winged are in the second.

questions.q: Put these parts of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Both, unskilled, unable, in their own work; then holding half the Veda; then like one-winged birds.

questions.q: Which word completes the invented line शिष्यौ ____ स्तः, the two pupils are unable?
optionExplain: This is singular; the line has two pupils.
This is plural; the line has two pupils.
Right: A dual noun takes a dual adjective ending in -औ.
This is neuter singular; the line has two pupils.
questions.explain: शिष्यौ is dual, so the describing word is dual: असमर्थौ.
questions.rule: A describing word agrees in number.
questions.teaches: A describing word agrees with its noun: dual noun, dual describing word, like उभौ अनिपुणौ.

questions.q: To what does the verse first compare herbs, before it turns with तु?
optionExplain: The weapon comes after the turn.
The thunderbolt comes after the turn.
Poison comes after the turn.
Right: ओषध्योऽमृतकल्पाः says herbs are like ambrosia.
questions.explain: The first comparison is ambrosia.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: ओषध्यः and अमृतकल्पाः are feminine nominative plural; अज्ञैः is instrumental plural.

questions.q: What does तु do in the first line?
optionExplain: Right: तु is glossed but and sets the two comparisons against each other.
The reason word is not तु here.
तु does not mean where.
There is no question in the verse.
questions.explain: तु means but and sets ambrosia against weapon, thunderbolt and poison.
questions.teaches: तु is an indeclinable meaning but; it sets two statements against each other.

questions.q: By whom do the herbs become like a weapon, a thunderbolt and poison?
optionExplain: The verse says the ignorant.
Right: अज्ञैः उपहृताः says this.
Kings are not mentioned.
Sages are not mentioned.
questions.explain: They become so when brought by the ignorant.

questions.q: Put these words in the order in which they stand in the verse (other words stand between them).
questions.explain: Herbs, like ambrosia, like weapon, thunderbolt and poison, by the ignorant, brought.

questions.q: What does the invented phrase शिष्यैः पठितम् mean?
optionExplain: For would be a dative idea.
From would be an ablative idea.
Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural by, as in अज्ञैः.
-ऐः is plural, not singular.
questions.explain: शिष्यैः is by the pupils, like अज्ञैः, by the ignorant.
questions.teaches: -ऐः on a masculine noun in -अ is the plural by: अज्ञैः, शिष्यैः.

questions.q: What word does the verse use for those who are ignorant of such procedures?
optionExplain: That would mean good physicians; the verse does not say it.
That means great sages, not named here.
That means pupils, not named here.
Right: It means bad physicians.
questions.explain: They are called कुवैद्याः, bad physicians.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: The two -आदिषु words are locative plural; लोभात् is ablative.

questions.q: At the end of a word like स्नेहादि, what does आदि add?
optionExplain: Right: The card glosses स्नेहादिषु as in oleation and the rest.
आदि widens; it does not limit.
The card gives and the rest.
Nothing here means without.
questions.explain: -आदि widens a single item to that and others of its kind.
questions.teaches: आदि at the end of a compound means beginning with, and the rest: स्नेहादि, छेद्यादि.

questions.q: What does the verse name as their motive?
optionExplain: Pity is not mentioned.
Right: लोभात् means from greed.
Fear is not mentioned.
Pride is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The motive named is greed.

questions.q: Put these words and phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: In oleation and the rest, ignorant who, in excision and the rest procedures, people, from greed, bad physicians.

questions.q: What does the invented phrase व्याकरणादिषु निपुणः mean?
options: Skilled in grammar and the rest.
Unskilled in grammar and the rest.
optionExplain: -आदि widens; it does not limit.
आदि here does not mean before.
Right: -आदिषु is in X and the rest, like स्नेहादिषु.
निपुण means skilled, not unskilled.
questions.explain: -आदिषु extends the field: grammar and the rest.
questions.teaches: X-आदिषु in the locative plural means in X and the rest.

questions.q: To what is the man who knows both compared?
optionExplain: The verse says two-wheeled.
The verse puts the chariot in battle.
Horses are not mentioned.
Right: द्विचक्रः स्यन्दनो यथा, in battle.
questions.explain: The comparison is a two-wheeled chariot in battle.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: अर्थसाधने and आहवे are locative singular; निर्वोढुम् is an infinitive.

questions.q: He is ____ (able) in accomplishing the aim. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: समर्थः is the masculine nominative singular: able.
questions.teaches: समर्थः = able.
questions.rule: The nominative names the man who is able.

questions.q: Which of these words describe the man who knows both?
optionExplain: Timid; not said of him in this verse.
Intelligent.
Unskilled; not said of him in this verse.
Able.
Knower of both.
questions.explain: He is the knower of both, intelligent and able.

questions.q: Put these parts of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Who knows both, intelligent, he able in accomplishing the aim, in battle to carry out the task, as a two-wheeled chariot.

questions.q: In the invented line शिष्यः पठितुं समर्थः, what does पठितुम् mean?
optionExplain: Right: -तुम् makes an infinitive, as in निर्वोढुम्.
That would be an absolutive.
That would be a gerundive.
That would be a noun of the doer.
questions.explain: पठितुम् is to read, the infinitive, like निर्वोढुम्.
questions.teaches: -तुम् added to a root gives the infinitive, to do: निर्वोढुम्, पठितुम्; समर्थ takes it, able to do.

questions.q: How much does the teacher teach at a time, according to the text?
options: A whole chapter, according to the pupil's wish.
A word, a quarter-verse or a verse, according to capacity.
Only a full verse, whatever the capacity.
A whole page, according to the season.
optionExplain: A chapter at once is not mentioned.
Right: पदं पादं श्लोकं वा, यथाशक्ति.
The text allows a word or a quarter-verse too.
Pages and seasons are not mentioned.
questions.explain: The portion is a word, a quarter-verse or a verse, according to capacity.

questions.q: Put the three portions the teacher may teach in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The text names the word, then the quarter-verse, then the verse.

questions.q: Match each word of the passage to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words describing the recital.
questions.rule: Each begins with a negating अ- or अन-.
questions.teaches: अ- (अन- before a vowel) negates the word that follows: अद्रुत, अनभिनीत.

questions.q: Which of these does the text say the recital must not be?
options: In tones neither too high nor too low.
optionExplain: सुसंस्कृतम् says it should be well formed.
अद्रुतम्: not hurried.
अविलम्बितम्: not delayed.
नात्युच्चैः: not too high.
The text asks for this: it is what is to be done, not what must not be.
questions.explain: Not hurried, not delayed and not too high are all said; well formed and neither too high nor too low are things to do.

questions.q: Put these parts of the passage in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The teacher teaches according to capacity, the portions are joined in order, one by one he puts them together, and himself recites after.

questions.q: By the pattern of अनुपठेत्, what does the invented अनुवदेत् mean?
optionExplain: अनु- does not mean against.
A negation would need अ- or न.
Right: अनु- means after and -एत् means should, as in अनुपठेत्.
-एत् is should, not a past ending.
questions.explain: अनुवदेत् is should say after, like अनुपठेत्, should recite after.
questions.teaches: अनु- before a verb means after, and the optative -एत् means should: अनुपठेत्, अनुवदेत्.

questions.q: What does the pupil reach, studying by this method?
optionExplain: No king is mentioned.
No seat is mentioned.
No night is mentioned.
Right: शास्त्रान्तमाप्नुयात् says this.
questions.explain: He would reach the end of the treatise.

questions.q: Put the pupil's four qualities in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Pure, devoted to the teacher, skilful, free from drowsiness and sleep.

questions.q: What does गुरुपरः say of the pupil?
options: He is devoted to the teacher.
He is greater than the teacher.
He is far from the teacher.
He is the teacher of others.
optionExplain: Right: The card marks a bahuvrihi: devoted to the teacher.
Nothing here says greater.
Nothing here says far.
He is called the pupil.
questions.explain: गुरुपरः is devoted to the teacher.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrihi with -पर describes someone intent on the first member: गुरुपर, devoted to the teacher.

questions.q: Which of these qualities does the verse give the pupil?
optionExplain: Drowsy: the verse says free from drowsiness.
Pure.
Sleepy: the verse says free from sleep.
Devoted to the teacher.
Skilful.
questions.explain: The verse gives pure, devoted to the teacher and skilful, and says free from drowsiness and sleep.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: विधिना is instrumental singular; शास्त्रान्तम् is accusative singular.

questions.q: By the pattern of तन्द्रानिद्राविवर्जितः, what does the invented भयवर्जितः mean?
optionExplain: -वर्जित takes away; it does not add.
Right: -वर्जित at the end of a compound means free from.
Giver would end in -द.
The word is a compound, not a genitive.
questions.explain: भयवर्जित = free from fear, like तन्द्रानिद्राविवर्जित = free from drowsiness and sleep.
questions.teaches: A compound ending in -वर्जित means free from the first member: भयवर्जित, free from fear.

questions.q: Who is told in this verse to strive?
options: One who has not begun study.
One who has reached the end of study.
optionExplain: The verse says reached the end.
The teacher is not mentioned.
Right: अध्ययनान्तगः says this.
The king is not mentioned.
questions.explain: He who has reached the end of study is told to strive.
questions.rule: अध्ययनान्तगः = one who has reached the end of study.

questions.q: Put the matters for which he should strive in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: Excellence of speech, knowledge of meaning, boldness, skill in work, practice, success.

questions.q: The one who has reached the end of study should ____ (strive). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: यतेत is the third person singular optative middle of the root यत्: should strive.
questions.teaches: यतेत = should strive.

questions.q: Which matter comes right after skill in practical work in the verse?
optionExplain: It comes before skill in work.
It comes earlier still.
It comes after practice, last.
Right: तदभ्यासे follows कर्मनैपुणे.
questions.explain: तदभ्यासे follows कर्मनैपुणे.
questions.rule: Read the list in its order.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the matters listed in the verse.

questions.q: What does the invented line शास्त्रविज्ञाने यतेत mean?
options: He should strive for knowledge of the treatise.
He should strive against knowledge of the treatise.
He should strive from knowledge of the treatise.
He strove for knowledge of the treatise.
optionExplain: Right: The locative after यतेत is read for, as in अर्थविज्ञाने.
The locative here is not against.
From would be an ablative.
यतेत is should strive, not a past form.
questions.explain: The locative after यतेत names what he strives for.
questions.teaches: After यतेत the locative names the aim: अर्थविज्ञाने, शास्त्रविज्ञाने.

questions.q: What do the speakers say they will do with the chapter?
optionExplain: No such verb appears in the line.
Right: व्याख्यास्यामः means we shall explain.
The verb is explain, not listen.
The form is future, not past.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः is the verb: we shall explain.

questions.q: Match each word of the opening to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four separate words once the joins are opened.
questions.rule: अथ and अतः are indeclinables; अध्यायम् is accusative; व्याख्यास्यामः is a future verb.

questions.q: We shall explain the Prabhashaniya ____ (chapter). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अध्यायम् is the accusative: the thing to be explained.
questions.teaches: अध्यायम् = chapter, the object of the explaining.

questions.q: Which of these words are indeclinables (marked ind. on the card)?
optionExplain: A verb form.
A noun in the accusative.
ind.: therefore.
ind.: now.
questions.explain: The card marks अथ and अतः as ind.; the other two change with case or person.

questions.q: Put the words of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The line runs: now, therefore, the Prabhashaniya, chapter, we shall explain.

questions.q: In the invented line वयं पठिष्यामः, what does पठिष्यामः mean?
optionExplain: Past would not use this ending.
They would need a third person ending.
Right: -ष्यामः is the same future ending as -स्यामः in व्याख्यास्यामः.
This ending is plural, so not I.
questions.explain: The ending -स्यामः / -ष्यामः is first person plural future.
questions.teaches: First person plural future: -स्यामः means we shall.

questions.q: What does this short unit do?
options: It gives a rule of surgery for pupils.
It lists the chapters of the whole work.
It names the students who are addressed.
It names the speaker whose words follow.
optionExplain: No subject-matter of that kind appears here.
No list appears in this unit.
Only the speaker is named.
Right: The unit holds only the speaker, and the sentence goes on.
questions.explain: The unit names Dhanvantari as the speaker; his words come in the next unit.
questions.rule: A speaker line precedes the speech.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Three words of the line.
questions.rule: भगवान् and धन्वन्तरिः are nominative; उवाच is the verb.

questions.q: The speaker is भगवान् ____. Type the name in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: The name stands in the nominative as the subject of उवाच.
questions.teaches: धन्वन्तरिः = Dhanvantari, the speaker.

questions.q: Which words are in the nominative singular (the doer)?
optionExplain: An indeclinable: as.
A verb: said.
m. nom. sg.: the speaker's name.
m. nom. sg.: describes the speaker.
questions.explain: Both भगवान् and धन्वन्तरिः are marked m. nom. sg.

questions.q: Put these words of the line in the order of the text (the joined opening opened into यथा and उवाच).
questions.explain: As, said, the revered one, Dhanvantari.

questions.q: By the sandhi in यथा + उवाच = यथोवाच, what does सदा + उवाच give?
optionExplain: Right: आ + उ becomes ओ, as in यथोवाच.
The उ cannot simply vanish.
आ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
The two vowels do join in this sandhi.
questions.explain: आ + उ = ओ in sandhi, exactly as यथा + उवाच = यथोवाच.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: आ + उ joins into ओ.

questions.q: The text compares unexpounded study to what?
options: A lamp in a closed room.
A seed sown in good soil.
optionExplain: No lamp is mentioned.
Right: खरस्य चन्दनभार इव.
No river is mentioned.
No seed is mentioned.
questions.explain: The simile is the donkey's load of sandal.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the line.
questions.rule: खरस्य is genitive singular; परिश्रमकरम् is a compound meaning causing toil.

questions.q: Mastered study, if not expounded, causes ____ toil (the word meaning only, alone). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: केवलम् is the indeclinable: only, alone.
questions.teaches: केवलम् = only.
questions.rule: केवलम् limits the result to toil alone.

questions.q: Under what condition does mastered study only cause toil?
options: When it has not been learned by heart at all.
When it has been learned only a single time.
When it is not expounded as to its meaning.
When it is not written down in any book.
optionExplain: The study is already mastered (अधिगतम्).
Nothing about the number of times.
Right: अप्रभाषितम् अर्थतः says exactly this.
Nothing about writing is said.
questions.explain: The condition is that the meaning is not expounded.
questions.rule: अप्रभाषितम् अर्थतः = not expounded in meaning.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Mastered study, not expounded, like a donkey's sandal-load, only toil.

questions.q: Using the अ- rule of अप्रभाषितम्, what does अपठितम् mean?
optionExplain: The prefix does not strengthen.
Nothing about reading aloud.
Nothing about repeating.
Right: अ- negates पठितम् (read), as in अ-प्रभाषितम्.
questions.explain: अ- before a consonant says not.
questions.teaches: The prefix अ- negates the word that follows.

questions.q: What does the donkey carrying sandal know?
options: The load, but not the sandal.
The sandal, but not the load.
Both the load and the sandal.
Neither the load nor the sandal.
optionExplain: Right: भारस्य वेत्ता न तु चन्दनस्य.
The words are reversed.
The sandal is exactly what it does not know.
It does know the load.
questions.explain: वेत्ता is the knower: of the load, not of the sandal.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: भारस्य and चन्दनस्य are genitive singular; मूढाः is nominative plural.

questions.q: The deluded carry treatises ____ (like a donkey). Type the word in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: खरवत् is खर + वत् (like); the printed text shows it as खरवद् before वहन्ति.
questions.teaches: -वत् = like.
questions.rule: -वत् builds a word meaning like X.

questions.q: Which rendering of the first line is right?
options: Like the donkey carrying sandal, who knows the sandal, not the load.
Like the donkey carrying sandal, who knows the load, not the sandal.
Like the donkey carrying a load, who knows neither load nor sandal.
Like the donkey carrying sandal, who knows sandal and load alike.
optionExplain: भार and चन्दन are swapped.
Right: It follows भारस्य वेत्ता न तु चन्दनस्य.
It does know the load.
The न तु rules out knowing the sandal.
questions.explain: The donkey is the knower of the load only.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: First the donkey, what it knows, what it does not, then the deluded and their carrying.

questions.q: By the -वत् rule, what does वृषभवत् वहति mean?
optionExplain: -वत् does not make an object.
-वत् does not change who acts.
Right: -वत् = like, as in खरवत्.
-वत् does not mean for.
questions.explain: वृषभवत् = like an ox.
questions.teaches: -वत् added to a noun means like that noun.

questions.q: How should the chapters be taken up, according to the text?
options: Summarised in brief, leaving out the many fine details.
Read silently and alone by the student, without any hearing.
Recited quickly in one go, without pausing on any of the words.
Recounted and listened to word by word and verse by verse.
optionExplain: The text asks for the opposite.
The text says recounted and listened to.
The text says word by word.
Right: अनुपदपादश्लोकम् अनुवर्णयितव्यम् अनुश्रोतव्यं च.
questions.explain: Both recounting and listening are asked for, in fine steps.
questions.rule: अनुपद- = word by word (avyayībhāva); अनु- here means each, along.

questions.q: Put the first five listed matters in the order in which the text names them.
questions.explain: The list begins: substance, taste, quality, potency, post-digestive change.

questions.q: Match each listed term to its plain sense on the card.
questions.explain: Plain senses only; the text does not define these terms here.
questions.rule: These are all named in the list of subtle matters.
questions.teaches: Plain meanings of terms the text lists.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT named among the subtle matters?
optionExplain: Right: No season is named in the list.
अस्थि is in the list.
मर्म is in the list.
स्नायु is in the list.
questions.explain: Bones, vital spots and sinews are listed; seasons are not.
questions.rule: Only named items belong to the list.

questions.q: Put the steps of the argument in the order of the text.
items: First conclusion: the chapters should be recounted and heard
Why? The listed matters are subtle
Pondered, they would confuse even a clear, vast intellect
How much more a little intellect
Conclusion repeated with the word necessarily
questions.explain: Conclusion, reason, strong case, stronger case, conclusion again.

questions.q: In the invented पण्डितोऽपि मुह्येत् किं पुनर्बालः, what does किं पुनः add?
options: A denial that the child is confused.
An even clearer case: how much more the child.
A question about who the child is.
A repeat of the first statement.
optionExplain: किं पुनः does not deny.
Right: किं पुनः = how much more, as in किं पुनरल्पबुद्धेः.
It is not asking for an identity.
It extends the point to a weaker case.
questions.explain: अपि sets the hard case; किं पुनः carries it further.
questions.rule: अपि ... किं पुनः = even ... how much more.
questions.teaches: किं पुनः argues a fortiori: if the strong case holds, much more the weak one.

questions.q: From whom should the explanation of such matters be heard?
options: Only from the author of this text.
Only from those who know those treatises.
From nobody, as it is self-evident.
optionExplain: The text sends the listener elsewhere.
The word एव limits it to the knowers.
Right: तद्विद्येभ्य एव व्याख्यानम् अनुश्रोतव्यम्.
The text says it must be heard.
questions.explain: एव (only) limits the source to those who know the treatises concerned.

questions.q: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four phrases of the unit.
questions.rule: एकस्मिन् शास्त्रे is locative; सर्वशास्त्राणाम् is genitive plural.

questions.q: What reason does the text give for this?
options: Other treatises are forbidden to read.
The matters are of no importance.
One treatise cannot comprise all treatises.
optionExplain: Nothing is forbidden here.
The text calls for hearing them.
Availability is not mentioned.
Right: नह्येकस्मिन् शास्त्रे शक्यः सर्वशास्त्राणामवरोधः कर्तुम्.
questions.explain: The reason is the limit of a single treatise.
questions.rule: न हि ... शक्यः = it is not possible.
questions.teaches: कस्मात् asks why; हि gives the reason.

questions.q: Which of these words are genitive plural?
optionExplain: Ablative plural: from the knowers.
Locative singular: in a treatise.
n. gen. pl.: of treatises.
m. gen. pl.: of matters.
questions.explain: The ending -नाम् / -णाम् marks the genitive plural here.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the unit in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Matters of other treatises, brought in here, heard from the knowers; why? Not in one treatise.

questions.q: By the locative rule of एकस्मिन् शास्त्रे, what does एकस्मिन् ग्रामे mean?
optionExplain: Right: -स्मिन् is the locative: in.
That would be the ablative.
That would be the genitive.
That would be the nominative.
questions.explain: -स्मिन् and -े both mark in.
questions.teaches: Locative singular: -स्मिन् on pronominal words like एक, -े on a-stem nouns (शास्त्रे, ग्रामे): in.

questions.q: What would one who studies a single treatise not know?
options: The settled conclusion of a treatise.
optionExplain: The verse says nothing of its name.
Right: न विद्याच्छास्त्रनिश्चयम्.
The verse says nothing of an author.
The verse says nothing of length.
questions.explain: शास्त्रनिश्चयम् is the object of न विद्यात्.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The one-treatise student, what he lacks, therefore, what the physician should do.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the verse.
questions.rule: विद्यात् and विजानीयात् are optative; अधीयानः is a participle.
questions.teaches: Optative and participle forms in the verse.

questions.q: Which words are optative (would, should)?
optionExplain: A noun: physician.
A participle: studying.
3 sg. opt.: should know thoroughly.
3 sg. opt.: would know.
questions.explain: The card labels both as opt.

questions.q: What does तस्मात् (therefore) in the second line rest on?
options: The earlier claim that every treatise is short.
Studying one single treatise is strictly forbidden to every physician.
One who studies a single treatise would not know the conclusion.
The physician must compose a new treatise of his own.
optionExplain: Length is not mentioned.
The verse does not forbid it.
Right: Because of तस्मात् after the claim.
Writing is not mentioned.
questions.explain: तस्मात् (therefore) links the second line to the first.

questions.q: In the invented स गच्छेत्, what does गच्छेत् mean?
optionExplain: A past would not use -एत्.
A plain present would be गच्छति.
That would be an absolutive.
Right: -एत् is the optative ending, like -यात् in विद्यात्.
questions.explain: -एत् is the optative: would or should.
questions.teaches: An optative ending gives the sense would or should.

questions.q: The verse calls one who works by the treatise a physician. What does it call the others?
optionExplain: Right: अन्ये तु तस्कराः.
The word is तस्कराः, not students.
The word is तस्कराः, not teachers.
The word is तस्कराः, not guests.
questions.explain: तस्कराः means thieves.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Taking up, attending, repeatedly, doing the work, he is a physician, the others thieves.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the verse.
questions.teaches: Absolutives and a few key words.

questions.q: Which words are absolutives (having done)?
optionExplain: A noun: thieves.
A present verb: does.
abs.: having attended on.
abs.: having taken up.
questions.explain: Both are marked abs. on the card.

questions.q: Which is NOT among the things the verse says the physician does?
optionExplain: आदाय says this.
Right: No teaching is mentioned.
उपास्य ... असकृत् says this.
कर्म कुरुते says this.
questions.explain: Taking up, attending and working are named; teaching is not.

questions.q: With the prefix उप-, which absolutive from नी (to lead) follows the pattern of उपास्य?
optionExplain: -त्वा is used without a prefix.
That is a participle, not an absolutive.
Right: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य.
That is a present verb.
questions.explain: A prefixed verb takes -य, as in आदाय and उपास्य.
questions.teaches: With a prefix, the absolutive ends in -य, not -त्वा.

questions.q: Of what does the verse call these four the roots?
options: Of the chapters of this work.
optionExplain: The Vedas are not mentioned.
The verse says surgical treatises.
Chapters are not mentioned.
Right: शेषाणां शल्यतन्त्राणां मूलानि.
questions.explain: The roots are of the remaining surgical treatises (शल्यतन्त्र).

questions.q: Put the four names in the order in which the verse lists them.
questions.explain: Aupadhenava, Aurabhra, Sushruta's, Paushkalavata.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the second line.
questions.rule: शेषाणाम् and शल्यतन्त्राणाम् are genitive plural.
questions.teaches: Genitive plural and optative in the second line.

questions.q: What does सौश्रुतम् denote in this list?
optionExplain: Right: A taddhita form: of Sushruta, with a work understood.
The form is an adjective of origin.
No pupil is mentioned.
No place is mentioned.
questions.explain: The card glosses it as (work) of Sushruta.

questions.q: Which word in the second line gives the verb of the sentence?
optionExplain: A genitive plural, not a verb.
Right: It is the optative verb of the line.
A noun, not a verb.
A genitive plural, not a verb.
questions.explain: निर्दिशेत् is the verb: one should indicate.

questions.q: Following the pattern of सुश्रुत → सौश्रुतम्, what is the form for of Kapila?
optionExplain: The first vowel is unchanged here.
अ lengthens to आ, not to ऐ.
Right: The first vowel is strengthened (वृद्धि): अ→आ, उ→औ; so क→का, as सु→सौ.
औ is the grade of उ, not of अ.
questions.explain: The pattern strengthens the first vowel: सु → सौ, पु → पौ, क → का.
questions.rule: पहला स्वर वृद्धि पाता है (सु→सौ, पु→पौ).
questions.teaches: Names of works strengthen the first vowel (वृद्धि).

questions.q: What do the speakers say they will do with the chapter?
optionExplain: No such verb appears in the line.
The verb is explain, not hear.
The form is future, not past.
Right: व्याख्यास्यामः means we shall explain.
questions.explain: व्याख्यास्यामः is the verb: we shall explain.

questions.q: Match each word of the opening to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the four separate words once the joins are opened.
questions.rule: अथ and अतः are indeclinables; अध्यायम् is accusative; व्याख्यास्यामः is a future verb.

questions.q: We shall explain the Agropaharaniya ____ (chapter). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: अध्यायम् is the accusative: the thing to be explained.
questions.teaches: अध्यायम् = chapter, the object of the explaining.

questions.q: Which of these words are indeclinables (अव्यय on the card)?
optionExplain: A verb form.
A noun in the accusative.
अव्यय: therefore.
अव्यय: now.
questions.explain: The card marks अथ and अतः as अव्यय; the other two change with case or person.

questions.q: Put the words of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The line runs: now, therefore, the Agropaharaniya, chapter, we shall explain.

questions.q: By the sandhi in अथ + अतः = अथातः, what does तथा + अत्र give?
optionExplain: Right: अ or आ followed by अ or आ joins into one long आ.
The long vowel does not shorten.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from अ + अ.
औ comes from अ + ओ or औ, not from अ + अ.
questions.explain: अ/आ + अ/आ = आ, exactly as अथ + अतः = अथातः.
questions.rule: Like vowels a/ā meeting give ā.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: अ/आ + अ/आ joins into a single long आ.

questions.q: What does this short unit do?
options: It gives a rule for an operation.
It names the speaker whose words follow.
It lists the chapters of the work.
optionExplain: No such subject-matter appears here.
Right: The unit holds only the speaker.
No list appears in this unit.
Only the speaker is named.
questions.explain: The unit names Dhanvantari as the speaker; his words come after it.
questions.rule: A speaker line precedes the speech.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Four words of the line once the join is opened.

questions.q: The speaker is भगवान् ____. Type the name in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: The name stands in the nominative as the subject of उवाच.
questions.teaches: धन्वन्तरिः = Dhanvantari, the speaker.

questions.q: Which words are in the nominative singular (the doer)?
optionExplain: An indeclinable: as.
A verb: said.
m. nom. sg.: the speaker's name.
m. nom. sg.: describes the speaker.
questions.explain: Both भगवान् and धन्वन्तरिः are marked m. nom. sg.

questions.q: Put the separate words of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The line runs: as, said, venerable, Dhanvantari.

questions.q: By the sandhi in यथा + उवाच = यथोवाच, what does तथा + उक्तम् give?
optionExplain: The two vowels do join in this sandhi.
आ + उ gives ओ, not औ.

questions.teaches: Sandhi: आ + उ joins into ओ.

questions.q: What does the text first state about procedure (कर्म)?
optionExplain: The word is threefold, not one.
The word is threefold, not two.
That number is not given for कर्म here.

questions.explain: The first word states that procedure is of three kinds.

questions.q: Match each term to its meaning.
questions.explain: Each name is a compound of an adjective-like first member and कर्म.
questions.rule: पूर्व = before, प्रधान = principal, पश्चात् = after.

questions.q: The third kind listed is the one done after the principal procedure: type its name in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma). ____
questions.explain: पश्चात्कर्म joins पश्चात् (after) and कर्म (procedure).
questions.teaches: पश्चात्कर्म = after-procedure, listed third.
questions.rule: पश्चात् as first member means after.

questions.q: Which of these are named by the text as kinds of procedure?
optionExplain: Not in this list.
Named: the after-procedure.
Named: the principal procedure.
Named: the preliminary procedure.
questions.explain: The list holds exactly three names: पूर्वकर्म, प्रधानकर्म, पश्चात्कर्म.

questions.q: Put the three kinds in the order in which the text lists them.
questions.explain: The list runs: preliminary, principal, after.

questions.q: By the pattern of प्रधानकर्म (principal procedure), what does प्रधानवैद्यः mean?
optionExplain: Right: The first member describes the second, as in प्रधानकर्म.
The compound is not a possessive pair.
वैद्यः is the head, not कर्म.
प्रधान means principal, not after.
questions.explain: In such a compound the first word qualifies the last: principal + physician.
questions.teaches: In a compound like प्रधानकर्म, the first member qualifies the last.

questions.q: Along with the operation itself, what will the text teach?
optionExplain: No such object appears.
Right: तत्सम्भारान् च: and its requisites.
No such object appears.
No such object appears.
questions.explain: The last phrase adds the requisites of the operation.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Five words of the line.
questions.rule: अस्मिन् and शास्त्रे are locative singular; तत्सम्भारान् is accusative plural.

questions.q: तत्सम्भारान् is accusative plural. What does the accusative tell us?
options: They are the ones who teach.
They are where it is taught.
They are what will be taught.
They are why it is taught.
optionExplain: The doer would be nominative.
A place would be locative.
Right: The accusative marks the object of उपदेक्ष्यामः.
A reason would not be a plain accusative.
questions.explain: The accusative names the object: what we shall teach.
questions.teaches: The accusative marks the thing acted upon.

questions.q: Which words in the line carry the sense of first?
optionExplain: ind.: and.
ind.: only, itself.
ind.: first.
ind.: first, to begin with.
questions.explain: तावत् and पूर्वम् both mean first; एव limits, and च adds.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the line in the order of the text.
questions.explain: In this science, the operation itself first, we shall teach first, and its requisites.

questions.q: By the ending in उपदेक्ष्यामः, what does the invented वयं द्रक्ष्यामः mean?
optionExplain: A past form would not end so.
They would need a third person ending.
This ending is plural, not I.
Right: -क्ष्यामः is a first person plural future ending.
questions.explain: The ending -स्यामः / -क्ष्यामः is first person plural future.
questions.rule: 1 pl. future ends in -स्यामः or its variants.
questions.teaches: First person plural future: उपदेक्ष्यामः is we shall teach.

questions.q: What does the text say is eightfold?
optionExplain: Right: शस्त्रकर्म अष्टविधम्.
Attendants are not mentioned here.
No diseases are listed here.
No chapters are counted here.
questions.explain: The surgical operation is said to be of eight kinds.

questions.q: Match each name of an operation to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five of the eight names, with the glosses of the card.
questions.rule: Each is a gerundive from a root, used as a name.

questions.q: The last operation named is ____ (suturing). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: सीव्यम् comes from the root सिव् and stands last in the list.
questions.teaches: सीव्यम् = suturing, the eighth name.

questions.q: Which of these are among the eight operations the text names?

Named: suturing.
Named: draining.
Named: extracting.
questions.explain: The text names extracting, draining and suturing; burning is not in the list.

questions.q: Put these five names in the order in which the text lists them.
questions.explain: The list runs: excising, incising, scraping, puncturing, probing, extracting, draining, suturing; these five are consecutive.

questions.q: By the pattern of छेद्यम् (to be cut), what does the invented पाठ्यम् mean?
optionExplain: A past participle would end in -ित.
Right: A gerundive in -य from the root पठ् gives what is to be read.
The doer would be a form like पाठकः.
A gerundive gives what is to be done.
questions.explain: A -य gerundive means what is to be done: पाठ्यम् = to be read.
questions.teaches: Gerundive in -य: root + य gives what is to be done.

questions.q: What does the text say is to be made ready beforehand?
options: A single instrument and nothing besides.
Only the names of the diseases.
A long list of articles and attendants.
Only the patient's family and friends.
optionExplain: The text gives a long list.
No diseases are listed here.
Right: पूर्वमेव उपकल्पयितव्यानि, then the list.
No family is named here.
questions.explain: The text lists many articles and then the qualities of the attendants.
questions.rule: उपकल्पयितव्यानि = are to be made ready.

questions.q: Match each article in the list to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Five names from the list, with the glosses of the card.
questions.rule: These are names only; the text states no use here.

questions.q: In this line, which word names the doer of the making ready?
optionExplain: Caustic is one of the things made ready.
Fire is one of the things made ready.
An indeclinable meaning beforehand.
Right: The instrumental names the doer of a gerundive.
questions.explain: With a gerundive the doer stands in the instrumental: वैद्येन, by the physician.
questions.teaches: With a gerundive in -तव्य, the doer stands in the instrumental.

questions.q: Which qualities of the attendants does the text name?
optionExplain: Not named in this line.
Named: strong.
Named: steady.
Named: kindly, affectionate.
questions.explain: The attendants are kindly, steady and strong.

questions.q: Put these five articles in the order in which the list begins.
questions.explain: The list begins: instruments, blades, caustic, fire, probe.

questions.q: By the -तव्य rule, what does the invented शिष्येण ग्रन्थः पठितव्यः mean?
options: The book is to be read by the student.
The student has read the book.
The student reads the book to us.
optionExplain: Right: -तव्य gives to be done; the doer is instrumental.
A past form would not use -तव्य.
-तव्य gives a duty, not a report.
The instrumental marks the student as doer.
questions.explain: पठितव्यः is to be read, and शिष्येण is by the student.
questions.rule: -तव्य = to be done, by the instrumental doer.
questions.teaches: -तव्य gerundive: to be done, with the doer in the instrumental.

questions.q: Up to what point does the text say the instrument is set in?
options: Until the fire is put out.
optionExplain: No count is given for this.
Right: आपूयदर्शनात्: up to the sight of pus.
The patient's speech is not mentioned.
The fire is only honoured here.
questions.explain: The phrase आपूयदर्शनात् says up to the sight of pus.

questions.q: Match each name of a part to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Five of the six names the physician is said to avoid.
questions.rule: The six words are a list in the accusative plural.

questions.q: The instrument is withdrawn ____ (once), says the text. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: सकृत् is once; with एव it reads सकृदेव, only once.

questions.rule: सकृत् limits the withdrawing to a single time.

questions.q: Which of these words are absolutives (having done)?
optionExplain: An optative: should withdraw.
An optative: should set in.
क्त्वा: having restrained.
ल्यप्: having seated.
क्त्वा: having honoured.
questions.explain: The card marks them क्त्वा or ल्यप् (having done); the two optatives are the main verbs.
questions.rule: Absolutive = having done, marked क्त्वा or ल्यप्.

questions.q: Put these five verb forms in the order in which the text states them.
questions.explain: The text runs: having honoured, having seated, having restrained, should set in, should withdraw.

questions.q: By the -त्वा rule, what does पठित्वा mean in the invented ग्रन्थं पठित्वा वदति?
optionExplain: That is the gerundive, not the absolutive.
A finite verb would end in -ति.
Right: Root + -त्वा gives having done, as in अर्चयित्वा.
The form states an earlier action.
questions.explain: पठित्वा is the absolutive: having read, before वदति.
questions.teaches: Absolutive: root + -त्वा (or -य after a prefix) gives having done.

questions.q: Of what are the qualities in this line said to be?
optionExplain: वैद्य is not the subject here.
No instrument is described here.
No attendant is mentioned here.

questions.explain: The closing phrase names the qualities of a wound.

questions.q: Match each quality to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Four of the named qualities, with the glosses of the card.

questions.q: How is निराश्रयः built, by the card?
optionExplain: Right: The card gives bahuvrihi: without lodgement.

The card shows a negative first member.

questions.q: Which of these are named as qualities of the wound in this line?

Not in this line.

Named: long.

questions.q: By the निर्- rule in निराश्रयः, what does the invented निर्भयः mean?
optionExplain: That would be भयवान्.
Right: निर्- = without, here with भय (fear).
The prefix does not mean of.
The prefix does not mean a little.
questions.explain: निर्भयः is without fear, built like निराश्रयः.

questions.q: What does the verse say is praised in the operation?
options: A wound kept open for as long as possible.
An instrument that is long and well-defined.
A long, broad, well-defined wound made on time.
A physician who is bold and well-trained.

The qualities belong to the wound, not an instrument.
Right: व्रणः कर्मणि शस्यते.
The qualities belong to the wound.
questions.explain: The verse praises the wound that has these qualities and is made in time.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: The four qualities are nominative; शस्यते is a passive verb.

questions.q: In the operation the wound ____ (is praised). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: शस्यते is the passive of the root शंस्: is praised.
questions.teaches: शस्यते = is praised.

Without lodgement: a quality of form.
In the operation: the place of the praise.
