questions.q: Put these qualities in the order in which the verse lists them.
questions.explain: The verse runs: long, broad, well-defined, without lodgement, made in time.

questions.q: What does the verse say is praised in the physician's surgical operation?
options: Patience, silence and a long delay before acting.
Courage, quick action and freedom from confusion.
Wealth, fame and a large following of students.
Anger, haste and a loud voice at the bedside.

Right: शौर्यम्, आशुक्रिया, असंमोहः are in the list.
None of these is listed.
None of these is listed.
questions.explain: The verse lists courage, quick action, a sharp instrument and freedom from confusion.

questions.q: Match each praised quality to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Four of the praised qualities.
questions.rule: Each stands in the nominative as a subject of शस्यते.

questions.q: What does the prefix अ- do in असंमोहः?

The prefix does not make a place.

The word remains a noun.

questions.q: By the अ- rule in असंमोहः, what does the invented अक्रोधः mean?

The prefix does not make a place.
The prefix does not mean cause.

questions.explain: अक्रोधः is not-anger, built like असंमोहः.
questions.teaches: अ- + noun gives the absence of that thing.

questions.q: What does the verb कुर्यात् mean?
optionExplain: Right: The card gives 3 sg. optative of the root कृ.
A past form would not be an optative.
The present would be करोति.
A passive would end in -यते or -ित.
questions.explain: कुर्यात् is the optative: should make.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning on the card.

questions.q: बुद्ध्या is instrumental. What does that case usually show?

questions.explain: The instrumental gives the means: with judgement.

questions.q: Which words are accusative plural on the card?

f. inst. sg.: with judgement.
m. acc. pl.: wounds.
m. acc. pl.: other.

questions.q: By the -य rule in अवेक्ष्य, what does the invented आनीय mean?

The prefix आ does not negate.

questions.explain: आनीय is the absolutive of आ + नी: having brought.
questions.teaches: After a prefix the absolutive ends in -य: having done.

questions.q: What two things does the verse tie the making of the wound to?
optionExplain: Neither is named in the verse.
Neither is named in the verse.
Neither is named in the verse.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning on the card.

questions.q: Wherever the track is found, ____ (there) the wound is made. Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: तत्र is the correlative of यत्र: there, where.

questions.rule: यत्र ... तत्र pairs where with there.

questions.q: What does the doubling in यतो यतो convey?
optionExplain: Right: Doubling gives the sense of every place.
Doubling spreads it, not narrows it.
No negative is attached to it.
It means each place, not repeating one.

questions.q: Put these four phrases of the verse in the order of the text.

questions.q: By the pattern of यत्र यत्र ... तत्र तत्र, what does यत्र यत्र वैद्यः गच्छति तत्र तत्र शिष्याः गच्छन्ति mean?
options: The physician goes only to one place.
Wherever the physician goes, there the students go.
Where the students go, the physician stays.
The students go, the physician does not.
optionExplain: Doubling spreads the sense, not narrows.
Right: यत्र यत्र ... तत्र तत्र = wherever ... there.
The roles are not reversed.
No such contrast is stated.
questions.explain: The doubled pair gives wherever ... there, in each case.
questions.teaches: Doubled यत्र and तत्र pair up: wherever ... there.

questions.q: Which of these places does the text name in its list?

No word for knee appears.

questions.q: Match each listed place to its meaning on the card.

questions.q: The list ends in -एषु. What does that locative plural ending mean for the whole list?

That would be the ablative.
That would be the dative.

Not named in this line.
Named: armpit.

questions.q: What shape of cut does the verse link with the hands and feet?

No such shape is named.
questions.explain: The hands and feet go with the moon-disc shape.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning on the card.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.

questions.q: In चन्द्रमण्डलवत्, what does the ending -वत् mean?

questions.q: Which rendering joins the shapes and the places correctly?

Half-moon in all four places named.
Moon-disc in hands and feet; half-moon in anus and penis.

questions.q: By the pattern of अर्धचन्द्राकृतीन्, what does the invented कमलाकृतयः (as in कमलाकृतयः छेदाः) mean?

questions.q: What does the text state follows when it is done otherwise?
options: Quick healing of the wound and freedom from all pain, in the end.
Cutting of veins and sinews, great pain, slow healing and fleshy growths.
A change of instrument, a change of diet and a change of the bandage.
Fever, thirst, weakness of the limbs and loss of sleep at night.
optionExplain: These are the opposite of what the text lists.
Right: The unit lists these four results after अन्यथा.
No such changes are listed.
None of these is named in the unit.
questions.explain: After अन्यथा the unit lists four results: cutting of veins and sinews, excessive pain, slow healing of the wound, and fleshy growths.
questions.rule: अन्यथा = otherwise; the results are listed.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: These are the five parts of the series once the joins are opened.
questions.rule: Each member of the series is a nominative; चिरात् is an indeclinable.

questions.q: Put the results in the order in which the text lists them.
questions.explain: The unit runs: cutting of veins and sinews, excessive pain, slow healing of the wound, fleshy growths.
questions.teaches: A series of results can be learned in the order the text gives them.

questions.q: Which of these does the unit state as results?
options: Healing of the wound at once
Healing of the wound after a long time
optionExplain: The text says after a long time, not at once.
सिरास्नायुच्छेदनम् is the first result.
अतिमात्रं वेदना is the second result.
चिराद्व्रणसंरोहः is the third result.
questions.explain: Three of the four are stated; the text says the wound heals only after a long time.

questions.q: Which split of चिराद्व्रणसंरोहः is right?
optionExplain: द्व्रण is not a word of the series.
आद्व्रण is not a word of the series.
Right: Final त् becomes द् before the voiced व.
The unit has no such form.
questions.explain: चिरात् (from a long time) joins with व्रणसंरोहः: त् turns into द् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: By the join in प्रादुर्भावः + च = प्रादुर्भावश्च, what is रामः + च?
optionExplain: The visarga becomes श् before च, not स्.
The visarga becomes ओ only before a voiced sound after अ.
The visarga does not simply vanish before च.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्, as in प्रादुर्भावश्च.
questions.explain: Visarga + च gives श्च, exactly as in प्रादुर्भावश्च.
questions.teaches: A visarga before च joins as श् (श्च).

questions.q: On what kind of patient does the text say the operation is done in these conditions?
options: On one who has not eaten.
On one who has eaten lightly.
On one who is fast asleep.
On one who has freshly bathed.
optionExplain: Right: अभुक्तवतः means of one who has not eaten.
The text says has not eaten.
Sleep is not mentioned.
Bathing is not mentioned.
questions.explain: The unit names the patient as one who has not eaten (अभुक्तवान्).
questions.rule: अभुक्तवतः = of one who has not eaten.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
pairs: of one who has not eaten
questions.explain: Five words of the unit.
questions.rule: मुखरोगेषु is a locative plural; अभुक्तवतः a genitive singular.

questions.q: Put the conditions in the order in which the text lists them.
questions.explain: The list runs: obstructed foetus, udara, arśas, aśmarī, bhagandara, mouth diseases.
questions.teaches: A list of names can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which of these conditions are named in the unit?
optionExplain: Not named in this unit.
Named fifth in the list.
Not named in this unit.
Named fourth in the list.
questions.explain: The list holds six names; भगन्दर and अश्मरी are among them, कुष्ठ and ज्वर are not.

questions.q: In अर्शोऽश्मरी, what does the sign ऽ stand for?
options: A long आ belonging to the word अर्श.
The initial अ of अश्मरी, dropped after ओ.
The visarga left over from the word अर्श.
A full stop that ends the sentence.
optionExplain: The sign ऽ does not mark a long vowel.
Right: अर्शः + अश्मरी: the अ after ओ is dropped and marked ऽ.
The visarga has already become ओ.
The sentence does not end there.
questions.explain: अर्शः + अश्मरी: the visarga becomes ओ before the soft अ, and the dropped अ is marked ऽ.

questions.q: By the join in मूढगर्भ + उदर = मूढगर्भोदर, what is सूर्य + उदय?
optionExplain: अ + उ does not give ऊ.
अ + उ gives ओ, not औ.
Right: अ + उ joins as ओ, as in मूढगर्भोदर.
The two vowels do join here.
questions.explain: अ + उ becomes ओ, so सूर्य + उदय = सूर्योदय.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: a short अ followed by उ joins as ओ.

questions.q: How does this long sentence mostly link its many acts?
options: With a separate short sentence for each single act.
With a list of nouns all standing in the genitive.
With questions put and answered, one after another.
With forms meaning having done, one after another.
optionExplain: It is one long sentence, not many short ones.
Most of the acts are verb forms, not genitive nouns.
The unit contains no questions.
Right: आश्वास्य, परिपीड्य and the rest are such forms.
questions.explain: The acts are chained by absolutives (having done), then the main verbs close the sentence.

questions.q: Match each form meaning having done to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five absolutives of the unit.
questions.rule: Prefixed verbs take -य; दत्त्वा has no prefix.

questions.q: Put these phrases in the order in which the text gives them.
questions.explain: The text runs: reassured, pressed with the finger, rubbed the wound, washed with a decoction, bind with a strip of cloth.
questions.teaches: A chain of absolutives gives the acts in the order they come.

questions.q: Which word is formed with -त्वा, since it has no prefix?
optionExplain: Right: √दा without a prefix: -त्वा.
It has the prefix परि, so it ends in -य.
It has the prefix प्र, so it ends in -य.
It has the prefix आ, so it ends in -य.
questions.explain: Only दत्त्वा lacks a prefix and ends in -त्वा.

questions.q: With what does the text say the wound is washed?
optionExplain: The strip of cloth is for binding.
Right: कषायेण प्रक्षाल्य.
The paste covers the wick; the washing is with a decoction.
Cold water is used to reassure the patient.
questions.explain: कषायेण प्रक्षाल्य: washed with a decoction.

questions.q: By the pattern of प्रक्षाल्य, what is the form meaning having sat down, from उप + √विश्?
optionExplain: -त्वा belongs to a verb without a prefix.
That is the present, he sits down.
Right: A prefixed verb takes -य.
That is a passive present form.
questions.explain: With the prefix उप the absolutive ends in -य: उपविश्य.
questions.teaches: With a prefix, the absolutive ends in -य, not -त्वा.

questions.q: In the translation of the card, what is done with the ghee that remains?
options: It is poured into the water-pot nearby.
It is mixed back into all the powders.
It is kept aside for use at a later time.
His prāṇas are touched with it (as rendered).
optionExplain: The water-pot is not named in this unit.
No mixing back is mentioned.
Nothing of the kind is said.
Right: आज्यशेषेण च अस्य प्राणान् समालभेत.
questions.explain: With the remaining ghee, the text states, his prāṇas should be touched.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the unit.
questions.rule: आज्य is ghee; शेष is what is left over.

questions.q: Put the names in the order in which the text lists them.
questions.explain: The list runs: guggulu, aguru, sarjarasa, vacā, pale mustard seed.
questions.teaches: A list of names can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which of these does the unit name together with the powders?
optionExplain: लवण: mixed in.
Not named in this unit.
निम्बपत्र: mixed in.
आज्य: joined to them.
questions.explain: The powders are mixed with salt and nimba leaves and joined with ghee; honey is not named here.

questions.q: Which split of गुग्गुल्वगुरु is right?
optionExplain: Right: उ before a different vowel becomes व्.
अ + अ would give आ, not व.
अगुरु is a word of the list.
आ + अ would give आ, not व.
questions.explain: गुग्गुलु (guggulu) and अगुरु (aguru) are two names; उ + अ joins as व.

questions.q: By the join in गुग्गुलु + अगुरु = गुग्गुल्वगुरु, what is साधु + अपि?
optionExplain: The vowels must join; they do not simply merge.
Right: उ before अ becomes व्.
उ + अ does not give ओ.
उ + अ does not give ऊ.
questions.explain: उ + अ gives व् + अ, so साधु + अपि = साध्वपि.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: उ before a different vowel becomes व्.

questions.q: What does the unit close by saying that we shall state?
optionExplain: No disease is named in this unit.
No student is mentioned here.
Right: तद्वक्ष्यामः: that we shall state, after रक्षाकर्म.
No instrument is named here.
questions.explain: तत् points back to the protective rite just mentioned; the unit ends by promising to state it.

questions.q: Match each word of the unit to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the unit.
questions.rule: गृहीत्वा is an absolutive; वक्ष्यामः is a first person plural future.

questions.q: Put the words in the order in which the text gives them.
questions.explain: The unit runs: from the water-pot, waters, having taken, sprinkling, protective rite.
questions.teaches: The order of the words follows the order of the acts.

questions.q: Which word means sprinkling, an act going on at the same time?
optionExplain: It means having taken, an earlier act.
It means we shall state.
It names the rite, not an act of sprinkling.
Right: A present participle in -न्: while doing.
questions.explain: प्रोक्षयन् is the present participle (sprinkling); गृहीत्वा is the earlier act (having taken).

questions.q: In तद्वक्ष्यामः, what does तत् stand for?
optionExplain: Right: रक्षाकर्म is neuter, like तत्.
उदकुम्भ is masculine, तत् is neuter.
The patient is not mentioned in this unit.
The wound is not mentioned in this unit.
questions.explain: तत् is neuter accusative and picks up रक्षाकर्म, the rite.
questions.rule: तत् points back to the thing just named.

questions.q: What does the invented sentence सः पठन् गच्छति mean?
optionExplain: That would need a form like पठित्वा.
Right: पठन् is a present participle: while reading.
No future form is used.
गच्छति is a verb, not an object.
questions.explain: A participle in -न् shows an act going on at the same time, like प्रोक्षयन्.
questions.teaches: A participle in -न् (पठन्, प्रोक्षयन्) means while doing.

questions.q: For what two purposes does the speaker say the rite will be performed?
options: To cure fever and the fear of death itself.
To please Brahmā and gain wealth for all.
To counter sorceries and the fear of rakṣases.
To honour teachers and the fear of kings.
optionExplain: Neither is named in the verse.
Brahmā is asked to approve, nothing about wealth.
Right: कृत्यानां प्रतिघातार्थं तथा रक्षोभयस्य च.
Neither is named in the verse.
questions.explain: The verse names two purposes: countering sorceries (कृत्याः) and the fear of rakṣases.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: Two are genitives, one is a future, one is a wish.

questions.q: May ____ approve the rite. Type the name in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: ब्रह्मा stands in the nominative as the one asked to approve.
questions.teaches: ब्रह्मा is the subject of the wish अनुमन्यताम्.
questions.rule: The nominative names the one asked to act.

questions.q: What kind of form is अनुमन्यताम्?
optionExplain: A plain statement would not use this ending.
The future is करिष्यामि, in the other line.
The verse has no past form.
Right: The ending -ताम् marks a wish or request.
questions.explain: अनुमन्यताम् is a 3rd person imperative: may he approve.

questions.q: Put the phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The verse runs: for countering sorceries, and for the fear of rakṣases, I shall perform the rite, may Brahmā approve it.

questions.q: What does the invented sentence पिता तद् अनुमन्यताम् mean?
options: The father does not approve it.
optionExplain: Right: The ending -ताम् is a wish, as in अनुमन्यताम्.
A past would not use this ending.
A future would end like करिष्यामि.
There is no negative word.
questions.explain: The same ending -ताम् makes it a wish: may the father approve it.
questions.teaches: A 3rd person imperative in -ताम् expresses a wish: may he.

questions.q: Who are asked to destroy those who attack?
options: The ancestors of the one addressed.
optionExplain: These are among the attackers, not the destroyers.
Right: ब्रह्माद्याः घ्नन्तु तान्.
The ancestors are among the attackers named.
Neither is named in this verse.
questions.explain: ब्रह्माद्याः, Brahmā and the others, are asked to destroy them.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: अभिद्रवन्ति is present; घ्नन्तु is a wish.

questions.q: Put the beings in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The verse runs: nāgas, piśācas, gandharvas, ancestors, yakṣas and rākṣasas.
questions.teaches: A list of names can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which of these beings are named in the verse?
optionExplain: Named fourth.
Not named in this verse.
Named first.
Named in the compound यक्षराक्षसाः.
questions.explain: Nāgas, ancestors and yakṣas are named; sages are not.

questions.q: Who is the subject of घ्नन्तु?
optionExplain: They are among the attackers.
It is the object, them.
Right: A nominative plural, matching the plural verb.
It is the one addressed, the object of the attack.
questions.explain: घ्नन्तु is plural, and its subject is ब्रह्माद्याः; तान् is what they destroy.

questions.q: In the invented line ये छात्राः पठन्ति तान् गुरुः पाठयतु, to whom does तान् point back?
options: To students who do not study.
optionExplain: गुरुः is the subject, not the object.
No books are mentioned.
ये छात्राः पठन्ति names those who study.
Right: ये ... तान् pairs a relative with its answer.
questions.explain: ये ... तान् links the students who study with them: may the teacher teach them.
questions.teaches: Relative and answer: ये names a group, तान् points back to it.

questions.q: In what state are they asked to protect?
optionExplain: Right: ते नमस्कृताः: they, honoured with salutation.
No feeding is mentioned.
Naming is not the state given.
Nothing about sending away is said.
questions.explain: They are asked to protect once they have been honoured with salutation (नमस्कृताः).

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.

questions.q: Put the places in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The verse runs: on the earth, in the atmosphere, in the directions, dwelling in the house-site.
questions.teaches: A list of places can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which word of the verse states the condition under which they are asked to protect?
optionExplain: It says what they are, night-wanderers.
Right: It describes they: when saluted.
It says where some of them dwell.
It is the verb: may they protect.
questions.explain: The condition is stated by नमस्कृताः; the other words say who they are or what they do.
questions.rule: A participle can give the condition.

questions.q: What does the ending of पृथिव्याम् show?
optionExplain: The genitive would be पृथिव्याः.
The ablative would be पृथिव्याः.
Right: f. loc. sg. on the card.
The vocative would be पृथिवि.
questions.explain: पृथिव्याम् is marked locative singular: on the earth.

questions.q: What does the invented sentence ते गृहे चरन्ति mean?
optionExplain: From would need the ablative.
To would need the accusative.
चरन्ति is plural, so not he.
Right: गृहे is a locative: in the house; चरन्ति as in the verse.
questions.explain: गृहे is a locative (in the house) and चरन्ति is they roam, as in the verse.
questions.teaches: A locative (-ए, -आम्, -षु) tells where something happens.

questions.q: Which of these does the second line ask to protect?
optionExplain: Right: पर्वताः are named at the start of the second line.
The Sun is not named in this verse.
The wind is not named in this verse.
The Moon is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The second line names mountains, rivers and oceans.
questions.rule: The line lists the subjects of पान्तु.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five subjects of the verse.

questions.q: Put these subjects in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: The verse runs: sages, royal sages, mountains, rivers, oceans.
questions.teaches: A list of subjects can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Why does the verse use सर्वाः with the rivers but सर्वे with the oceans?
options: Rivers are many and oceans are few.
Rivers are feminine and oceans masculine.
Rivers are singular and oceans plural.
Rivers are near and oceans far away.
optionExplain: Both words are plural.
Right: सर्व takes the gender of its noun.
Both nouns are plural.
The endings show gender, not distance.
questions.explain: नद्यः is feminine and सागराः masculine, and सर्व agrees with each.
questions.rule: An adjective agrees with its noun in gender.

questions.q: Which split of पर्वताश्चैव is right?
optionExplain: The word is पर्वताः, with a visarga.
आश्च is not a word of the verse.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्; अ + ए gives ऐ.
श्च is not a word.
questions.explain: पर्वताः (mountains) + च (and) + एव (indeed) = पर्वताश्चैव.
questions.rule: Visarga + च = श्च; अ + ए = ऐ.

questions.q: By the join in च + एव = चैव, what is तथा + एव?
optionExplain: अ + ए gives ऐ, not ए.
The ए cannot simply vanish.
ओ does not arise from ए.
Right: अ or आ followed by ए joins as ऐ.
questions.explain: आ + ए joins as ऐ, as in च + एव = चैव.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: अ or आ followed by ए joins as ऐ.

questions.q: Which power does the verse ask to protect the breaths (प्राणान्)?
optionExplain: Right: प्राणान् वायुः: the breaths, Vāyu.
Soma is paired with the vyāna breath.
Parjanya has the last verb परिरक्षतु.
Indra is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: The verse pairs Vāyu with the prāṇa breaths.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: Two nouns name what is guarded, three name the protectors.

questions.q: Put these words in the order in which the verse gives them.
questions.explain: The words run: tongue, breaths, Vāyu, Soma, vyāna, Parjanya.
questions.teaches: Protectors and what they guard can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which powers are named in the verse?
optionExplain: Not named in this verse.
Named in the first line.
Named in the second line.
Named in the second line.
questions.explain: Vāyu, Soma and Parjanya are named; Varuṇa is not.

questions.q: What does the visarga of वायुः become in वायुस्तथैव?
optionExplain: श् appears before च, not before त.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्.
र् appears before a voiced sound.
ओ appears after अ before a voiced sound.
questions.explain: वायुः + तथा + एव = वायुस्तथैव: the visarga turns into स् before त.

questions.q: How do you say in Sanskrit: may the rivers protect you?
optionExplain: A singular subject does not take the plural verb.
A plural subject does not take the singular verb.
Right: A plural subject takes the plural wish पान्तु.
That is a statement, not a wish.
questions.explain: A plural subject goes with पान्तु, a singular one with पातु or रक्षतु.
questions.teaches: The wish ending agrees in number with its subject.

questions.q: Who is asked to protect the udāna breath?
optionExplain: The thunders go with the samāna breath.
The rivers are not named in this verse.
The mountains are not named in this verse.
Right: उदानं विद्युतः पान्तु.
questions.explain: The lightnings (विद्युतः) are asked to protect the udāna.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: उदानम्, समानम् and बलम् are accusatives.

questions.q: Put these words in the order in which the verse gives them.
questions.explain: The words run: udāna, lightnings, samāna, thunders, strength, Indra.
questions.teaches: What is protected and its protector can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which of these are named in the verse?
optionExplain: Named in the first line.
Not named in this verse.
Named in the second line.
Named in the first line.
questions.explain: Lightnings, thunders and Indra are named; Parjanya is not.

questions.q: What does the visarga of बलपतिः become in बलपतिर्मनुः?
optionExplain: Right: A visarga after इ before a voiced sound becomes र्.
स् appears before त or थ.
श् appears before च or छ.
ओ appears only after अ.
questions.explain: बलपतिः + मनुः = बलपतिर्मनुः: after इ the visarga turns into र् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: By the join in बलपतिः + मनुः = बलपतिर्मनुः, what is कविः + गच्छति?
optionExplain: स् does not stand before a voiced sound.
Right: Visarga after इ before a voiced sound becomes र्.
The visarga does not simply vanish here.
ओ arises only after अ.
questions.explain: After इ the visarga turns into र् before a voiced sound: कविर्गच्छति.
questions.teaches: A visarga after इ or उ becomes र् before a voiced sound.

questions.q: Whom does the verse ask to guard your sattva?
optionExplain: Varuṇa is paired with wisdom.
They are paired with desires.
Right: सत्त्वमिन्द्रोऽभिरक्षतु.
The ocean is paired with the navel region.
questions.explain: Indra is asked to guard the sattva.
questions.rule: Nominative = protector; accusative = what is guarded.

questions.q: Match each protector to what it is asked to guard.
questions.explain: The four pairs of the verse.
questions.rule: Each protector is a nominative, each guarded thing an accusative.

questions.q: Put the four phrases in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs: desires and the Gandharvas, sattva and Indra, wisdom and Varuṇa, the navel region and the ocean.
questions.teaches: Four pairs can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which pairing does the verse state?
optionExplain: Desires go with the Gandharvas.
Wisdom goes with Varuṇa.
Sattva goes with Indra.
Right: प्रज्ञां ते वरुणो राजा.
questions.explain: Wisdom (प्रज्ञा) is paired with King Varuṇa.
questions.rule: Match each protector with what it guards.

questions.q: Which split of कामांस्ते is right?
optionExplain: Right: न् before त joins as ंस्.
A visarga would give कामास्ते.
म् would give कामान्ते or कामंते.
The word is कामान्, ending in न्.
questions.explain: कामान् (desires, accusative plural) + ते (your) join as कामांस्ते.

questions.q: How do you say in Sanskrit: may Indra protect your wisdom?
optionExplain: The guarded thing needs the accusative प्रज्ञाम्.
Right: The guarded thing is accusative, the protector nominative.
Indra is one, so not a plural subject.
A singular subject takes the singular verb.
questions.explain: Use the pattern of the verse: accusative for what is guarded, nominative for the protector.
questions.teaches: The protector stands in the nominative and what it guards in the accusative.

questions.q: Who is asked to protect your mind?
optionExplain: The Sun is paired with the eye.
The directions are paired with the two ears.
Right: चन्द्रमाः पातु ते मनः.
The stars are paired with the form.
questions.explain: The Moon is asked to protect the mind.

questions.q: Match each protector to what it is asked to guard.
questions.explain: Four pairs of the verse.
questions.rule: Each protector is a nominative, each guarded thing an accusative.

questions.q: Put the four pairs in the order of the verse.
questions.explain: The verse runs: eye and Sun, directions and two ears, Moon and mind, stars and form.
questions.teaches: Four pairs can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: What does the ending of श्रोत्रे show about the ears?
options: The ears belong to the Moon.
optionExplain: A singular would be श्रोत्रम्.
A plural would be श्रोत्राणि.
The ears belong to the one addressed, ते.
Right: The card marks श्रोत्रे as dual.
questions.explain: A dual ending names two, so श्रोत्रे means the two ears.

questions.q: Which words make the verb of the second line plural (पान्तु)?
optionExplain: Right: Both are plural subjects.
रूपम् is singular and तव is a pronoun.
Neither is a plural subject.
Neither is a plural subject.
questions.explain: The subjects of the second line are नक्षत्राणि and निशाः, both plural.

questions.q: By the pattern of श्रोत्रे, what does नेत्रे in सूर्यः नेत्रे पातु show?
optionExplain: A singular would be नेत्रम्.
Right: A neuter dual in -ए, like श्रोत्रे.
A plural would be नेत्राणि.
Nothing in the form is negative.
questions.explain: A neuter dual ends in -ए, so नेत्रे means the two eyes, as श्रोत्रे means the two ears.
questions.teaches: A neuter dual ending in -ए (श्रोत्रे, नेत्रे) names two.

questions.q: What does the last word of the verse, वसुन्धरा, name?
optionExplain: The Moon is not named in this verse.
The ocean is not named in this verse.
Right: The English of the card glosses it as Earth.
The wind is not named in this verse.
questions.explain: वसुन्धरा is glossed Earth.

questions.q: Match each word of the verse to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: Four are natural things, one is a part of the body.

questions.q: Put these words in the order in which the verse gives them.
questions.explain: The words run: waters, body hairs, herbs, space, Earth.
questions.teaches: A list of names can be learned in the order of the text.

questions.q: Which of these natural things are named in the verse?
optionExplain: Not named in this verse.
Named in the first line.
Named at the end.
Named in the first line.
questions.explain: Herbs, waters and Earth are named; the ocean is not.

questions.q: Which split of रोमाण्योषधयः is right?
optionExplain: रोमाण is not the word; the word is रोमाणि.
The word is ओषधयः, not औषधयः.
उ + ओ would give व, not य.
Right: इ before ओ becomes य्.
questions.explain: रोमाणि (body hairs) + ओषधयः (herbs) join as रोमाण्योषधयः.

questions.q: By the join in रोमाणि + ओषधयः, what is दधि + ओदनम्?
optionExplain: Right: इ before ओ becomes य्.
The vowels must join.
इ + ओ does not give औ.
The इ does not vanish.
questions.explain: इ followed by a different vowel turns into य्: दधि + ओदनम् = दध्योदनम्.
questions.teaches: Sandhi: इ before a different vowel becomes य्.

questions.q: In this verse, which one is asked to protect the two eyebrows?
optionExplain: Vishnu is asked to protect the prowess.
Right: ध्रुवो भ्रुवौ: Dhruva and the two eyebrows.
Brahma is asked to protect the self.
Vaishvanara (fire) protects the head.
questions.explain: Dhruva is paired with the two eyebrows (भ्रुवौ).
questions.rule: Each name is paired with one thing protected.

questions.q: Match each one invoked to what he is asked to protect.
questions.explain: The pairs are शिरः, पराक्रमम्, आत्मानम्, भ्रुवौ in the order of the verse.

questions.q: Put the ones invoked in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: Fire and Vishnu in the first line; the best of men, Brahma and Dhruva in the second.
questions.teaches: The five invoked names run in a fixed order across the two lines.

questions.q: Which of these words name what is protected (accusative on the card)?
optionExplain: m. nom. sg.: the protector.
m. nom. sg.: the protector.
m. acc. sg.: the prowess.
n. acc. sg.: the head.
questions.explain: शिरः and पराक्रमम् are accusative; ब्रह्मा and ध्रुवः are nominative, the protectors.

questions.q: On the card, how is विष्णुस्तव split?
optionExplain: The card gives तव (your), not a word स्तव.
There is no word स्तव in the verse.
Right: A visarga before त becomes स्: Vishnu, your.
Vishnu is the protector, not an object.
questions.explain: विष्णुः + तव joins as विष्णुस्तव: a visarga before त becomes स्.

questions.q: Following this pattern, what does the invented चन्द्रो मुखं पातु mean?
options: May the face protect the Moon.
May the Moon protect the face.
optionExplain: The roles are swapped.
पातु is a wish, not a past.
The face is the object, not the Moon.
Right: चन्द्रः is the protector (nominative), मुखम् the thing protected, पातु a wish.
questions.explain: The nominative names the protector, the accusative the thing protected, and पातु makes it a wish.
questions.rule: Nominative protects accusative; पातु = let him protect.
questions.teaches: Protector in the nominative, protected in the accusative, पातु for a wish.

questions.q: What does the verse say about these deities and your body?
options: They are ever present in it.
They are absent from it and must be called.
They stay in it for a single day only, and then go.
They are present in the head alone.
optionExplain: Right: देहे विशेषेण ... नित्या हि देवताः.
The verse says they are present.
The word नित्याः means constant.
The verse says in the body, देहे.
questions.explain: नित्याः (constant) and देहे (in the body) say that they are ever present there.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Five words of the verse.
questions.rule: नित्याः and देवताः are feminine plural; देहे is locative.

questions.q: May they protect you ____ (continually). Type it in Devanagari or in English letters (e.g. dharma).
questions.explain: सततम् is the indeclinable: continually.
questions.teaches: सततम् = continually.
questions.rule: सततम् says how long the protection is wished for.

questions.q: Which of these words are plural on the card?
optionExplain: 2 sg. imp.: may you obtain, singular.
f. nom. pl.: the deities.
loc. sg.: in the body, singular.
3 pl. imp.: let them protect.
questions.explain: देवताः and पान्तु are plural; अवाप्नुहि and देहे are singular.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: First where the deities are, then the wish for protection, then the wish for long life.

questions.q: Patterned on पान्तु, what does गच्छन्तु mean in the invented ते गच्छन्तु?
optionExplain: One person would need गच्छतु.
Right: -न्तु is the 3rd person plural imperative, as in पान्तु.
A past is not made with -न्तु.
That would be a 2nd person form.
questions.explain: -न्तु = let them, as in पान्तु.
questions.teaches: The ending -न्तु makes a 3rd person plural wish: let them.

questions.q: What are Brahma and the others here asked to make for you?
optionExplain: No wealth is mentioned.
No victory is mentioned.
Right: स्वस्ति ते is repeated in every clause.
No fame is mentioned.
questions.explain: Each clause begins with स्वस्ति, well-being.

questions.q: Match each name to its meaning.
questions.explain: Names from the three lines.
questions.rule: चन्द्रसूर्यौ and नारदपर्वतौ are pairs in the dual.

questions.q: Put these invoked ones in the order in which the unit names them.
questions.explain: Brahma and the gods come first, then the two pairs of the second line, then Agni and Vayu in the third.
questions.rule: Order of the text; the last group of the third line is left out.
questions.teaches: The invoked names follow one another with the same word स्वस्ति.

questions.q: Which of these words are dual (two) on the card?
optionExplain: m. nom. sg.: one.
dvandva, m. nom. du.: Moon and Sun.
dvandva, m. nom. du.: Narada and Parvata.
m. nom. pl.: many.
questions.explain: The two pairs are marked du.; ब्रह्मा is singular and देवाः plural.

questions.q: How does the card split the start of स्वस्त्यग्निश्चैव?
optionExplain: The word is स्वस्ति; the इ is not lost without trace.
There is no word ग्निः.
There is no word स्वस्त्य here.
Right: इ before a different vowel becomes य्: svasti + agni.
questions.explain: स्वस्ति + अग्निः joins as स्वस्त्यग्निः (in स्वस्त्यग्निश्चैव), because इ before a different vowel becomes य्.

questions.q: Patterned on चन्द्रसूर्यौ, what does the invented पुत्रपौत्रौ mean?
optionExplain: Right: A dvandva in the dual: two named persons.
The ending -औ is dual, not plural.
A dvandva joins, it does not link by of.
The dual names two, not three.
questions.explain: A dvandva in -औ names two things together, as in चन्द्रसूर्यौ.
questions.rule: Dvandva dual: A and B, two.
questions.teaches: A dvandva in the dual names two things together.

questions.q: By whom does the verse say this protection was made?
optionExplain: The verse names the Grandsire.
Right: पितामहकृता: made by the Grandsire.
No king is mentioned.
No pupil is mentioned.
questions.explain: पितामहकृता means made by the Grandsire.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the verse.

questions.q: Put these wishes in the order in which the verse gives them.
questions.explain: The protection, well-being and life, the subsiding of afflictions, freedom from distress.
questions.teaches: The verse moves from protection to increase, to subsiding, to freedom from distress.

questions.q: Which of these words are imperatives (a wish or command) on the card?
optionExplain: 3 sg. imp.: let it increase.
A noun: protection.
3 pl. imp.: let them subside.
2 sg. imp.: be.
questions.explain: The first three are marked imp.; रक्षा is a noun.

questions.q: What happens to the इ of स्वस्ति when आयुः follows, as at the start of the printed स्वस्त्यायुर्वर्धतां?
optionExplain: The इ does not vanish; it becomes य्.
ए comes from अ + इ, not from इ + आ.
Right: svasti + ayuh: इ + आ gives या.
इ becomes य्, not व्.
questions.explain: इ before a different vowel becomes य्, so स्वस्ति + आयुः = स्वस्त्यायुः.

questions.q: Patterned on गतव्यथः, what does the invented गतभयः describe?
options: One who has gone to fear.
optionExplain: A bahuvrihi describes a person, not the thing itself.
That reverses the compound.
No place is meant.
Right: A bahuvrihi: one who has gone-fear, free from fear.
questions.explain: As गतव्यथः means one whose distress has gone, गतभयः means one whose fear has gone.
questions.rule: Bahuvrihi: one whose X has gone.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrihi with गत names a person whose X has gone.

questions.q: What does the speaker wish for the one addressed at the end of the verse?
optionExplain: Right: दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुहि: may you obtain a long life.
No wealth is mentioned.
No honour is mentioned.
No sons are mentioned.
questions.explain: The last words wish a long life: दीर्घम् आयुः.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the verse.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The mantras, the speaker, the one protected, the wish for long life.
questions.rule: Order of the text; the damaged word between the first and second phrase is left out.
questions.teaches: The verse names the means, the speaker, the one protected and the wish.

questions.q: Which of these words are instrumental (by, with) on the card?
optionExplain: m. inst. pl.: with these.
nom. sg.: you.
inst. sg.: by me.
2 sg. imp.: may you obtain.
questions.explain: एतैः and मया are marked inst.; त्वम् is nominative and अवाप्नुहि a verb.

questions.q: Who is described as कृतरक्षः in the second line?
options: The speaker, who has made the protection.
The mantras, which have made the protection.
The Veda, whose protection is made.
optionExplain: The speaker is मया, by me, not त्वम्.
Right: कृतरक्षः stands with त्वम्: you, whose protection is made.
The mantras are in the instrumental.
The Veda is not the one protected.
questions.explain: कृतरक्षः (bahuvrihi) agrees with त्वम्: you, whose protection is made.
questions.rule: Bahuvrihi + त्वम् = you, who have X.

questions.q: In the invented दीपैः गृहं शोभते, what does दीपैः mean?
optionExplain: -ऐः is plural, not singular.
Of would be the genitive.
Right: -ऐः is the instrumental plural, as in एतैः मन्त्रैः.
To would be the dative.
questions.explain: -ऐः makes the instrumental plural: with lamps, as मन्त्रैः means with mantras.
questions.teaches: The ending -ऐः on a plural noun means with or by.

questions.q: What is done with the protected patient, according to this unit?
options: He is sent away from the house.
He is taken into a forest.
He is left at the gate.
He is brought into the house.
optionExplain: The text says into the house.
No forest is mentioned.
No gate is mentioned.
Right: आगारं प्रवेश्य: having caused to enter the house.
questions.explain: प्रवेश्य with आगारम् means having caused him to enter the house.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the sentence.
questions.rule: प्रवेश्य is an absolutive; आतुरम् and आगारम् are accusative.

questions.q: Put these words of the sentence in the order of the text.
questions.explain: Then, the protected patient, the house, having caused to enter, he should instruct.
questions.rule: Order of the text; the doubtful word before the verb is left out.
questions.teaches: The sentence puts the absolutive before the main verb: having done, he should instruct.

questions.q: Which of these words are accusative singular on the card?
optionExplain: abs.: having caused to enter.
ind.: then.
m. acc. sg.: the protected one.
n. acc. sg.: the house.
questions.explain: कृतरक्षम् and आगारम् are accusative; प्रवेश्य is an absolutive and ततः an indeclinable.

questions.q: Why does प्रवेश्य end in -य and not in -त्वा?
optionExplain: Right: The card marks it as abs. of प्र-विश्.
The card marks it as an absolutive.
An absolutive does not change for number.
A wish would be an imperative.
questions.explain: A verb with a prefix forms its absolutive in -य: प्र + वेश्य.

questions.q: Patterned on प्रवेश्य, what is the absolutive, having sat down, of उप + विश् (to sit)?
optionExplain: -त्वा is not used with a prefix.
Right: With a prefix the absolutive ends in -य.
That is a participle, not an absolutive.
That is a present verb.
questions.explain: A prefixed verb takes -य, as in प्रवेश्य.
questions.teaches: With a prefix, the absolutive ends in -य, not -त्वा.

questions.q: On which day does the text state it is untied and bound again?
optionExplain: The text says the third.
The text says the third.
Right: तृतीयेऽहनि: on the third day.
The text says the third.
questions.explain: तृतीये अहनि means on the third day.
questions.rule: तृतीये अहनि = on the third day.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the sentence.
questions.rule: विमुच्य is an absolutive; बध्नीयात् is an optative.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the sentence in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The third day, untying, binding the same way, then the prohibition.
questions.teaches: The sentence gives the steps first, then the prohibition with न.

questions.q: Which of these are optative forms (he should) on the card?
optionExplain: 3 sg. opt.: he should bind.
abs.: having untied.
pres. part.: hurrying.
3 sg. opt. caus.: he should release.
questions.explain: बध्नीयात् and मोक्षयेत् are optative; the other two are not finite verbs.

questions.q: How does the card split तृतीयेऽहनि?
optionExplain: The card gives तृतीये, the locative.
A visarga here would not give ए.
The word is तृतीये, not तृतीया.
Right: Final ए before अ stays and the अ is marked ऽ.
questions.explain: तृतीये + अहनि joins as तृतीयेऽहनि, with the avagraha ऽ for the dropped अ.

questions.q: Following तृतीये + अहनि, what is गृहे + अपि written as?
optionExplain: Right: ए stays and the अ is marked ऽ, as in तृतीयेऽहनि.
ए does not become आ.
ए + अ does not give ऐ.
ए does not become य here.
questions.explain: Final ए before अ stays, and ऽ marks the dropped अ.
questions.teaches: Final ए before अ stays and the अ is replaced by ऽ.

questions.q: What does the text state follows release on the second day?
options: It heals early and without any pain.
It heals late and is severely painful.
It dries up and the patient grows weak.
It is unchanged and nothing follows.
optionExplain: The text says late and painful.
Right: चिरादुपसंरोहति तीव्ररुजश्च: heals late, severe pain.
Neither result is mentioned.
The text lists three results.
questions.explain: The text states healing late and severe pain (and a further word, विग्रथित, whose sense varies).
questions.rule: Result of release on the second day.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the sentence.

questions.q: Put these parts of the sentence in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The cause first, then the three results one after another.
questions.teaches: The cause is named first, then the results in a fixed order.

questions.q: Which of these words carry the sense from or after (ablative) on the card?
optionExplain: ind. (abl.): after a long time.
m. nom. sg.: the wound.
n. abl. sg.: from release on the second day.
3 sg. pres.: becomes.
questions.explain: The first two are marked abl.; व्रणः is nominative and भवति a verb.

questions.q: How does the card split तीव्ररुजश्च?
optionExplain: There is no word श्च.
The card gives the visarga form.
Right: A visarga before च becomes श्.
The words are तीव्ररुजः and च.
questions.explain: तीव्ररुजः + च joins as तीव्ररुजश्च: a visarga before च becomes श्.

questions.q: Patterned on तीव्ररुजः, what does the invented दीर्घकेशः describe?
optionExplain: A bahuvrihi describes a person, not the hair.
No cutting is meant.
The compound names a possessor.
Right: A bahuvrihi: having X, as तीव्ररुजः is having severe pain.
questions.explain: As तीव्ररुजः means having severe pain, दीर्घकेशः means having long hair.
questions.teaches: A bahuvrihi names the one who has the quality.

questions.q: Before the list, what does the text say he considers?
options: The doshas, the time, the strength, etc.
The patient's name, village and his family.
The phase of the moon and the stars.
The price, the weight and the place.
optionExplain: Right: दोषकालबलादीन् अवेक्ष्य.
None of these is named.
None of these is named.
None of these is named.
questions.explain: अवेक्ष्य (having considered) governs दोष, काल, बल and the like.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the sentence.

questions.q: Put the five matters in the order in which the text lists them.
questions.explain: Decoctions, plasters, bandaging, diet, conduct.
questions.teaches: The five matters come in one fixed list.

questions.q: Which of these does the text name among the five?
optionExplain: Named: bandaging.
Named: diet.
Not named in the list.
Named: plasters.
questions.explain: Plasters, bandaging and diet are named; bathing is not.
questions.rule: Only named items belong to the list.

questions.q: How does the card print अतः + ऊर्ध्वम्?
optionExplain: ओ comes from the visarga only before a voiced consonant or a short अ.
Right: A visarga after अ before a vowel other than अ drops; the vowels stay apart.
The vowels do not merge in this way.
The visarga does not become र् here.
questions.explain: After अ, a visarga before ऊ drops and no further joining happens.

questions.q: In the invented अश्वगजरथान् पश्यति, what does the dvandva अश्वगजरथान् name?
options: The horse of the elephant's chariot.
optionExplain: A dvandva does not link by of.
All members count, not only the first.
Right: A dvandva names all its members as the objects.
It lists separate things.
questions.explain: A dvandva lists all its members together, as the five matters of the text.
questions.teaches: A dvandva names all its members together, as separate things.

questions.q: What does the text say he should not do while hurrying?
options: Bind it with a cloth bandage.
Instruct him in the rules of conduct.
Make it heal with a fault within.
optionExplain: Binding is not mentioned here.
Instruction is not mentioned here.
Entering the house is not mentioned here.
Right: सान्तर्दोषं रोपयेत् is what he should not do.
questions.explain: न ... सान्तर्दोषं रोपयेत् forbids causing it to heal with a fault within.
questions.rule: न ... रोपयेत् = should not make it heal.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the sentence.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the sentence in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The prohibition, hurrying, the fault within, then the reason.
questions.teaches: The prohibition comes first and the reason follows with हि.

questions.q: What does हि do in स हि अल्पेन अपि अपचारेण?
options: It gives the reason: for, because.
It turns the clause into a question.
optionExplain: Right: The card glosses हि as for.
हि does not ask.
न is the word for not.
हि gives a reason, not a condition.
questions.explain: हि introduces the reason for the caution.

questions.q: Which of these words are instrumental singular (by) on the card?
optionExplain: 3 sg. opt. caus.: he should heal.
m. inst. sg.: by a slight.
m. inst. sg.: by a lapse.
ind.: again.
questions.explain: अल्पेन and अपचारेण are marked inst.; रोपयेत् is a verb and भूयः an indeclinable.

questions.q: Following च + एनम् = चैनम्, what does तदा + एव give?
optionExplain: A short sound is not made from आ + ए.
Right: अ or आ + ए gives ऐ.
The vowels do join.
आ + ए does not give ओ.
questions.explain: अ or आ before ए joins as ऐ: च + एनम् = चैनम्, तदा + एव = तदैव.
questions.teaches: अ or आ followed by ए joins into ऐ.

questions.q: Which of these does the text list among things to avoid even after healing?
optionExplain: Sleep is not named.
Bathing is not named.
Right: अजीर्ण is named in the list.
Conversation is not named.
questions.explain: अजीर्ण (indigestion) is the first item avoided; sleep, bathing and talk are not named.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words from the lines.
questions.rule: रूढे is locative; यावत् introduces the limit.

questions.q: Put the things the text lists to avoid in the order in which it names them.
questions.explain: Indigestion, exertion and the like come first, then joy, anger and fear.
questions.teaches: The things to avoid are listed in one fixed order.

questions.q: Which of these feelings does the unit name as to be avoided?
optionExplain: Grief: not named.
m. acc. sg.: joy, excitement.
m. acc. sg.: anger.
n. acc. sg.: fear.
questions.explain: Joy, anger and fear are named; grief is not.
questions.rule: Only named items belong to the list.

questions.q: Which is the right joining of तस्मात् and अन्तर्?
optionExplain: The अ is not lost and त् does not become न्.
The final त् is voiced before a vowel.
A य does not appear here.
Right: A final त् before a vowel becomes द्.
questions.explain: तस्मात् + अन्तर् is printed तस्मादन्तर्: the final त् becomes द् before a vowel.

questions.q: Patterned on रूढे (when healed), what does the invented गते मित्रे mean?
options: To the friend who has gone.
optionExplain: Right: A participle in the locative can mean when it has become so.
To would be the dative.
गते is a participle, not a present verb.
By would be the instrumental.
questions.explain: A locative participle, as in रूढे, states the time: when it has happened.
questions.rule: Locative participle = when it has happened.
questions.teaches: A participle in the locative can mean when the thing has happened.

questions.q: What does the verse give for each group of seasons?
options: The kind of cloth to be used.
A number of days to wait.
The place where to release it.
optionExplain: No cloth is named.
Right: त्र्यहात् and द्व्यहात् are after three days and after two days.
No place is named.
No physician is named.
questions.explain: Each group of seasons is given a number of days.
questions.rule: त्र्यहात् / द्व्यहात् = after three / two days.

questions.q: Match each season to its meaning.
questions.explain: Season names of the verse.
questions.rule: हेमन्त and वसन्त are locative; शरद्, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा are members of one locative compound.

questions.q: Put the seasons in the order in which the verse names them.
questions.explain: Three seasons in the first line, then the three of the second line.
questions.teaches: The six seasons run in one order, in two groups of three.

questions.q: By the order of the words, which seasons does the verse pair with release after two days?
optionExplain: Autumn: in the second group.
Summer: in the second group.
The cold season: in the first group, after three days.
The rains: in the second group.
questions.explain: The second group is autumn, summer and the rains.
questions.rule: द्व्यहात् goes with the second group.

questions.q: How is द्व्यहात् + शरद् joined in the verse?
optionExplain: The two words do join by sandhi.
The त् is not simply dropped.
Right: त् before श becomes च्, and श becomes छ्.
त् becomes च् before श, not द्.
questions.explain: A final त् before श becomes च् and the श becomes छ्: द्व्यहाच्छरद्.

questions.q: Patterned on वर्षासु (in the rains), what does the invented लतासु mean?
optionExplain: -आसु is plural.
From would be the ablative.
Of would be the genitive.
Right: -आसु is the locative plural of a feminine word in -आ.
questions.explain: A feminine -आ word takes -आसु in the locative plural: वर्षासु, लतासु.
questions.teaches: The locative plural of a feminine -आ word ends in -आसु.

questions.q: What comparison does the verse use for acting quickly?
optionExplain: Right: प्रदीप्तागारवत्: like a burning house.
No river is mentioned.
No tree is mentioned.
No sea is mentioned.
questions.explain: प्रदीप्त-आगार-वत् means like a burning house.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the verse.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The kind of disease, the thing not wished, the comparison, then the action.
questions.teaches: The first line says what not to wish; the second says what to do.

questions.q: Which of these words are locative plural on the card?
optionExplain: m. acc. sg.: the rule.
f. acc. sg.: the treatment.
m. loc. pl.: in rapidly advancing.
m. loc. pl.: in diseases.
questions.explain: अतिपातिषु and रोगेषु are locative plural; the other two are accusative singular.

questions.q: How are न and इच्छेत् joined in this verse?
optionExplain: ऐ comes from अ + ए, not from अ + इ.
Right: अ + इ gives ए.
The अ does not simply vanish.
The joining does not double the च.
questions.explain: न + इच्छेत् joins as नेच्छेत्, because अ + इ becomes ए.

questions.q: Patterned on प्रदीप्तागारवत्, what does the invented पर्वतवत् स्थिरः mean?
optionExplain: In would be the locative.
-वत् does not make a subject.
Right: -वत् means like.
-वत् here means like, not having.
questions.explain: -वत् added to a word gives like: पर्वतवत् = like a mountain.
questions.teaches: -वत् added to a noun means like that noun.

questions.q: What does the verse name as poured, slightly warm, over the pain?
optionExplain: Neither is named.
Neither is named.
Neither is named.
Right: घृतेन ... कोष्णेन यष्टीमधुकान्वितेन.
questions.explain: The verse names slightly warm ghrita joined with yashtimadhuka.

questions.q: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explain: Words of the verse.
questions.rule: जन्तोः is genitive; शान्तिम् is accusative.

questions.q: Put these phrases of the verse in the order of the text.
questions.explain: The pain and its cause, how it torments, then the calm and what is poured.
questions.teaches: The first line describes the pain; the second gives what the text states about its calm.

questions.q: Which of these words agree with वेदना (feminine nominative singular)?
optionExplain: n. acc. sg.: the body.
m. gen. sg.: of a creature.
f. nom. sg. p.p.: poured.
f. nom. sg.: severe.
questions.explain: तीव्रा and सिक्ता are feminine nominative singular like वेदना.
questions.rule: Adjectives agree in case, number and gender.

questions.q: What does the compound शस्त्रनिपातजाता say about the pain?
options: It has arisen from the fall of a weapon.
It has fallen on a weapon.
It has been born of a weapon's cure.
It will arise at the fall of a weapon.
optionExplain: Right: शस्त्र-निपात-जाता: born of the fall of a weapon.
The weapon is the cause, not the place.
No cure is the cause.
जाता is a past participle: arisen.
questions.explain: जाता (arisen) with शस्त्रनिपात (fall of a weapon): arisen from it.
questions.rule: Compound: arisen from the fall of a weapon.

questions.q: Patterned on घृतेन, what does वस्त्रेण in the invented वस्त्रेण आच्छादितः mean?
optionExplain: Of would be the genitive.
Right: -एन / -एण is the instrumental singular: with, by.
In would be the locative.
From would be the ablative.
questions.explain: The instrumental -एण, as -एन in घृतेन, means with or by.
questions.teaches: The instrumental singular ending -एन / -एण means with or by.
